chapters.title: The Wings That Burned
chapters.shortDesc: Argus speaks as the rejected twin: born beside Rafaela, hidden by the Church, and finally claimed by the Abyss.
chapters.fullDesc:
"They say I was born a mistake. A male angel, a contradiction in the sacred texts, a flaw in the divine design. My sister, Rafaela, was celebrated. They built statues in her honour, sang hymns to her mercy, begged for her healing touch. I was hidden. Shunned. Told that my light was too harsh, my power too dangerous, my existence an embarrassment to the Church."

Argus said those words to a priest who asked why he turned from the Light. He did not speak like a demon gloating over ruin. He spoke like a son reciting the shape of an old wound.

There is a particular silence that falls over a cathedral at midnight. It is not peace. It is stone holding its breath, stained glass watching without mercy, old prayers clinging to the air like dust. Argus knew that silence before he knew kindness. He knelt beneath gilded icons and received nothing but cold indifference.

He was born beside Rafaela in the Monastery of Light, a fortress of white stone, golden braziers, and marble halls where the Church trained its most devoted servants. Their mother, Elena, was a human peasant forced into a holy-water ritual that should have killed her. Instead, it gave her twins infused with celestial power.

Rafaela emerged glowing with soft golden light. Her first cry was a melody that made the monks weep. She was beautiful, graceful, and perfect: white-gold wings, luminous skin, gentle eyes, the kind of angel the Church wanted to display.

Argus emerged in force. His light was not warm. It was harsh, blinding, almost painful. His first cry shattered windows. Even as an infant, his presence felt like judgment rather than mercy.

The monks celebrated Rafaela as a blessing. They hid Argus like a shameful relic. He grew in the shadow of his sister's radiance, loving her even while watching the world give her everything he was denied.

Rafaela tried to protect him. She visited him in secret, bringing food, stories, and soft words. But the Church's cruelty was older than either of them, and its will was absolute.

Bitterness grew. The hunger for vengeance grew. The Abyss, ever watchful, found the cracks in his soul and poured itself in.

Argus became the Dark Angel: a fallen twin, a creature of shadow and flame, and a living reminder that even the Light can create monsters when it refuses to love what it has made.

chapters.title: The Ritual of the Holy Water
chapters.shortDesc: Elena, a displaced peasant girl, is chosen by the Sacrists and forced into a ritual that creates Argus and Rafaela.
chapters.fullDesc:
The Monastery of Light kept many secrets. The most sacred, and most shameful, was the ritual of the holy water. It dated back to the first days of the Church, when the Lord of Light's power was wild and untamed. The Sacrists believed that by infusing mortal women with divine essence, they could create vessels of celestial power: healers, warriors, symbols, weapons.

The women were never asked if they consented.

Argus and Rafaela's mother was a peasant named Elena, a young woman from a village destroyed by a demon incursion. She was slight, brown-haired, and hollow-eyed from grief, with work-roughened hands and a faded linen dress given to her by the monastery. The monks called their charity mercy. Then they told her she owed a debt.

The Sacrists chose her when she was eighteen. They wore layered white vestments stitched with gold thread, polished masks over their faces, and rings that glittered with holy sigils. They brought Elena to the inner sanctum, where the Lord of Light's presence was said to burn strongest, held her down, and poured holy water down her throat.

She screamed. The water burned like molten gold.

For three days she lay in fever, her body warring with the divine essence. On the fourth day the fever broke, and she was pregnant.

The gestation was unlike any natural pregnancy. Elena could feel two presences inside her: one warm and gentle, one hot and fierce. She spoke to them, sang to them, and begged them to be kind to each other.

The birth was catastrophic. Elena died moments after the twins emerged, her body unable to withstand the celestial energy that had consumed her.

Rafaela was placed in a silk-lined bassinet, surrounded by monks who cooed and praised. Argus was placed in a wooden crate, hidden in a storage room, forgotten among sacks of grain and cracked ceremonial vessels.

He was three days old before anyone remembered to feed him.

chapters.title: The Golden Sister and the Forgotten Brother
chapters.shortDesc: Rafaela grows adored and radiant while Argus is locked below the monastery, fed scraps, and taught to disappear.
chapters.fullDesc:
Rafaela's childhood was a procession of blessings. The monks adored her. Pilgrims crossed the empire to receive her benediction. She was taught by the finest scholars, trained by the most patient masters, and dressed in robes of white silk trimmed with gold. Her wings were kept clean, her hair braided with ribbons, her hands guided toward healing.

She grew kind, gentle, and compassionate: everything an angel was supposed to be.

Argus's childhood was different. He was given a cell in the lowest level of the Monastery, a damp, windowless room that smelled of mould, old straw, and neglect. He was fed scraps, clothed in rough grey cloth, and trained by monks who flinched whenever his power flared.

They did not know what to do with him. His light was too strong, too wild. When he tried to heal, he burned. When he tried to bless, he frightened people. When he tried to pray, the walls trembled.

"Monster," the younger monks whispered.

"Aberration," the older ones agreed.

Argus learned to hide his power. He learned to be small, quiet, invisible. He learned that survival meant pretending he did not exist.

Rafaela visited whenever she could. As a child she came barefoot, golden hair loose, carrying bread wrapped in napkins stolen from the dining hall. As she grew older, she came in white healer's robes, her luminous wings folded tight so they would not brush the dirty walls.

"You are not a monster," she told him. "You are my brother. I love you."

Argus wanted to believe her. He tried. But the Church's whispers were louder than her love, and every locked door taught him the same lesson: Rafaela was a miracle. Argus was a mistake.

chapters.title: The Scars That Never Healed
chapters.shortDesc: The monks attempt to purify Argus with holy fire, then use him as a deniable weapon when they fail.
chapters.fullDesc:
The scars on Argus's body were not from honest battle.

They were from the monks who tried to purify him: to burn the darkness out of his soul with holy fire, to beat the corruption from his flesh with blessed rods, to force his harsh light into a shape they could approve of. They called it therapy. Argus called it torture.

The purification chamber was a narrow room of white stone and iron restraints. Its walls were carved with prayers. Its floor was stained where holy water, blood, and ash had mixed too many times. The monks who worked there wore plain robes beneath leather aprons, their faces solemn, their hands steady.

They believed cruelty became sacred if performed in the name of the Light.

Argus endured it for years. Each session left him weaker, more hollow, more convinced that whatever goodness lived in the Church had never been meant for him. But the darkness never left. It only grew.

Eventually the monks gave up. They declared Argus incorrigible, a lost cause, a failure of their teachings. They stopped trying to save him and began to use him.

He was sent on the most dangerous missions: assassinations that required deniability, executions that could not be traced back to the Church, massacres that needed a scapegoat. He killed because he was ordered to kill. He had no other purpose.

Each mission took a piece of his soul. He watched light fade from the eyes of heretics, rebels, and innocents, and felt less each time.

The Abyss noticed his emptiness.

"You are alone," it whispered. "You have always been alone. They do not love you. They never will. But we can give you power. Power to make them fear you. Power to make them regret every cruelty."

Argus listened. He had nothing else to listen to.

chapters.title: The Breaking Point
chapters.shortDesc: The massacre of Thornhaven breaks Argus when one surviving child looks up and asks if he is an angel.
chapters.fullDesc:
The mission that broke Argus was the massacre of Thornhaven.

The Church declared the villagers heretics. They had refused tithes, questioned the priests' authority, and dared to pray to old gods beneath the trees instead of the Lord of Light beneath stained glass. For that, they were to be eliminated.

Argus was sent alone. He was ordered to kill everyone: men, women, children, elders, witnesses.

He obeyed.

He killed farmers in their fields, mothers in their homes, children in their beds. Thornhaven had been a small village of timber houses, muddy lanes, and hanging lanterns. By dawn it was a field of smoke and bodies.

When it was over, Argus stood in the village square with blood on his hands and nothing in his eyes.

A child had survived. She was no more than five, small and thin, with tangled dark hair and a patched yellow dress. She crawled out from a cupboard where someone had hidden her. She looked up at Argus with no fear, only confusion.

"Are you an angel?" she asked.

Argus could not answer.

He left her alive. It was the first time he had disobeyed an order.

The Church was furious. They threatened dungeons, excommunication, and purification rituals. Argus barely heard them. The child's question echoed louder than any priest.

Are you an angel?

He was not an angel. He was a monster. Worse, he was a monster made by those who called themselves holy.

And he was tired of being one.

chapters.title: The Whispers of the Abyss
chapters.shortDesc: The Abyss speaks gently to Argus, naming his pain and offering the power to never be hurt again.
chapters.fullDesc:
The Abyss found Argus in the aftermath.

It did not come as a demon with claws, a shadow with teeth, or a monster from a child's nightmare. It came as a voice: soft, soothing, almost maternal. It spoke in the quiet moments, when Argus sat alone in his cell and stared at the ceiling until the stones blurred.

"You have been wronged," the voice said. "You have been used. They made you a weapon, then blamed you for being sharp."

"I know," Argus whispered.

"They fear you. They have always feared you. Not because you are evil, but because you are different."

"I know."

"They will never accept you. No matter how many missions you complete, how many heretics you kill, how many villages you burn, they will always see you as a mistake."

Argus closed his eyes. The voice was right. It had always been right.

"What do you want me to do?" he asked.

"Come to us. We will give you power beyond anything the Church can offer. We will make you strong enough to never be hurt again. We will give you the vengeance you deserve."

The cell did not change. The damp walls remained. The rusted cot remained. The faint smell of ash and old prayers remained.

But something inside Argus shifted.

He would go to the Abyss. He would take its power. He would become the monster the Church had always feared.

And he would make them pay.

chapters.title: The Transformation
chapters.shortDesc: In the deepest catacombs, Argus carves abyssal symbols into his flesh and rises as the Dark Angel.
chapters.fullDesc:
The ritual was performed in the deepest catacombs of the Monastery, a place where the Light had never reached.

The walls were black with old damp. Forgotten bones lay in niches carved before the Church became powerful enough to hide its dead elsewhere. Argus descended alone, carrying a blade blessed by the Abyss and the words the voice had taught him.

He carved symbols into his own flesh. Each mark burned cold. Each chant made his throat ache and his teeth throb. He spoke until his voice became a rasp.

The Abyss answered.

Darkness poured into him, not gently and not kindly, but like a flood. His skin darkened to bruised purple. His eyes turned crimson beneath the first glow of green corruption. His wings, once white and gold, withered as feathers fell away and dissolved into ash. In their place grew ragged membranes of shadow and smoke.

He screamed. It was the sound of a soul being unmade and remade.

When it was over, he was no longer Argus the failed angel. He was something new. Something terrible. Something free.

He rose from the catacombs with dark wings spread and red eyes blazing. The monks who saw him ran. The ones who did not run died. He killed the priests who tortured him, the Sacrists who forced holy water down Elena's throat, and the monks who had whispered monster and aberration.

He did not kill Rafaela. He could not.

She stood in the courtyard, golden wings spread, healing light blazing around her white robes. Her eyes held no fear. Only sorrow.

"Brother," she said. "Please. Come back."

"I cannot," Argus replied. "There is nothing to come back to."

He flew into the night. The Monastery burned behind him.

He did not look back.

chapters.title: The Anatomy of a Fallen Angel
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed portrait of Argus: bruised-purple skin, green abyssal fire, ragged wings, silver armour, and the Demonic Blade.
chapters.fullDesc:
To look at Argus is to see a being of terrible beauty.

He stands just over six feet tall, with a physique that balances celestial grace and demonic power. He is not bulky; he has never needed brute force alone. His body is dense, lean, and battle-hardened, built by centuries of violence.

His face is the face of an angel unmade. The jawline is sharp and chiselled, suggesting aristocratic origins that the Church tried to bury. His cheekbones are high and severe. His skin is a deep bruised purple, almost cosmic, contrasting sharply with the toxic green energy that leaks from his core, arm, and weapon.

His head is encased in a high-set silver helmet, less a helm than a ceremonial crown-visor. Two prominent horns curve upward, their tips glowing with internal green fire. His face is hidden behind a vertical grate-style visor with three luminous green slits where eyes should be.

His torso is protected by heavy silver plating over organic-looking purple musculature. His right shoulder carries a massive multi-layered silver pauldron with sweeping blade-like protrusions. His left arm appears infected, jagged crystalline green growths erupting from bicep and forearm like abyssal thorns.

His lower body is draped in a long split-waist surcoat falling to mid-calf: matte charcoal outside, brilliant acidic green within. A heavy silver belt with a central diamond-shaped buckle holds it in place. Sleek articulated greaves guard his shins and knees, ending above exposed clawed feet.

His wings are massive and ragged, feathered near the base but dissolving into smoky shadow at the edges.

His weapon is a colossal single-edged curved greatsword, forged from the same corrupted green crystal that scars his arm. Bone-like protrusions line the spine near the hilt. Ghostly green flame coils around the blade.

The sword is named the Demonic Blade.

It hungers for life.

chapters.title: Demonic Blade - The Edge That Drains
chapters.shortDesc: Argus channels abyssal hunger into his sword, turning wounds into stolen life and pain into endurance.
chapters.fullDesc:
Demonic Blade is Argus's signature technique: a charge that builds over time, draining life from enemies to sustain his own.

The technique is a manifestation of his Abyssal nature. Argus channels corrupted energy into his greatsword, and the green flame intensifies, crackling with hunger. When he strikes, the blade does not merely cut. It drinks.

Life force pulls from the wound in thin streams of green-black light, flowing into Argus's body and knitting torn flesh, sealing cracks in armour, and feeding the corruption that keeps him standing.

Demonic Blade is not exhausting in the ordinary sense. Argus can use it as often as he has the strength to channel. But each use deepens his bond with the Abyss. Each stolen breath reminds him that survival has become another form of hunger.

He has learned to use the technique to sustain himself in battle. Against one enemy, it is cruel. Against many, it is terrifying. A battlefield that should weaken him can instead become a feast.

Enemies who face Argus quickly learn the horror of fighting something that grows stronger from their wounds.

He does not apologise for it.

The Church taught him to be a weapon. The Abyss taught him to endure.

chapters.title: Eternal Evil - The Immortality That Defies Death
chapters.shortDesc: Argus’s ultimate technique lets him refuse death for a few terrible seconds, turning rejection into temporary immortality.
chapters.fullDesc:
Argus's ultimate technique is Eternal Evil: a transformation that makes him immune to death for a short time, his life unable to fall below its final ember while his attacks and charges become supercharged.

It is the culmination of everything Argus is: fallen angel, Abyssal vessel, and unwanted child who was promised he would never be helpless again.

When he invokes Eternal Evil, he spreads his shadow wings and the darkness around him solidifies into armour. Green fire burns through the cracks in his body. The Demonic Blade howls. His visor flares so brightly that enemies see three green lines in their nightmares long after the battle ends.

For a few seconds, he cannot die. Blades pass through him without ending him. Spells break against his skin. Arrows strike, blood falls, bones crack, and still he moves forward.

The technique is exhausting. Each use drains Argus's reserves completely, leaving him weakened once the immortality fades. He can use it only once in a battle, and only if he has conserved enough power beforehand.

But when he uses it, he uses it with all the fury of a being told he should never have existed.

Eternal Evil is not courage. It is refusal.

It is Argus telling death to wait.

chapters.title: The War Against the Light
chapters.shortDesc: Argus leads attacks against the Church while Rafaela tries to stop him, each sibling unable to defeat or abandon the other.
chapters.fullDesc:
Argus leads Abyssal forces against the Church of Light.

He attacks monasteries, cathedrals, and pilgrimage routes. He kills priests, paladins, and worshippers caught beneath banners they may not understand. He does not discriminate. The Light is his enemy, and all who serve it become targets.

The Church paints him as a demon, and for once it is not entirely wrong. Yet every cathedral he burns carries memories: the smell of incense, the scrape of stone under bare knees, the sound of monks whispering monster where a child could hear.

Rafaela tries to stop him.

She appears on battlefields in white and gold, healing light blazing, wings spread wide enough to shield the wounded behind her. Her face is gentle, but grief has sharpened it. Her staff glows with holy radiance. Her voice trembles only when she says his name.

"I cannot be helped," Argus tells her. "I cannot be saved. I am what they made me."

"We can find a way," she insists. "Together."

"There is no together anymore. There is only me and the darkness."

They fight. Neither can defeat the other. Argus is stronger, but Rafaela is precise, disciplined, and stubborn with love. Each encounter leaves them wounded, exhausted, and more certain of their path.

Around them, armies clash. Between them, the old bond remains unbroken and unbearable.

chapters.title: The Sister's Tears
chapters.shortDesc: Rafaela keeps praying for Argus. He tells her to stop, but her prayers are the one warmth he cannot ignore.
chapters.fullDesc:
Rafaela has not given up on Argus.

She prays for him every night. She lights candles, offers sacrifices, and begs the Lord of Light to spare his soul. She does not know if her prayers are heard. She does not know if they matter.

But she prays anyway.

Sometimes, in the quiet moments between battles, Argus feels those prayers. They are like warmth in the cold, light pressing gently against the darkness inside him. He tries to ignore them. He cannot.

Rafaela looks nothing like the frightened monks who raised them. She is tall and radiant, her golden hair falling around her face, her white robes trimmed with holy gold, her wings bright enough to soften shadows. Yet when she looks at Argus, she is not a saint, not a symbol, not the Church's perfect miracle.

She is his sister.

"Stop praying for me," he says when they meet on a battlefield littered with broken stone and dying fire. "I do not deserve your prayers."

"You are my brother," she replies. "You will always deserve my prayers."

He turns away. He does not want her to see the tears in his eyes.

Argus tells himself those tears are weakness. The Abyss tells him they are chains. But some part of him, buried beneath purple skin and green flame, knows the truth.

They are proof that something human remains.

chapters.title: The Legacy of the Dark Angel
chapters.shortDesc: Argus does not know whether vengeance will free him, but he will keep fighting the world that rejected him.
chapters.fullDesc:
Argus does not know what the future holds.

He does not know if he will ever defeat the Church. He does not know if he will ever be free of the Abyss. He does not know if Rafaela will ever smile at him again without sorrow in her eyes.

But he knows what he will do in the meantime.

He will fight. He will burn. He will never stop.

The blade never dulls. The wings never tire. The vengeance never ends.

He is Argus, the Dark Angel, and he will never forgive the world that rejected him.

His legacy is not simple evil. It is a warning carved in green fire across the history of the Church: do not call cruelty holy and expect the wounded to remain obedient. Do not create a weapon and act surprised when it cuts the hand that forged it.

To the faithful, he is a nightmare. To the Abyss, he is proof that the Light can be broken. To Rafaela, he is still her brother.

To himself, Argus is less certain.

He only knows that the sky feels colder now, and his wings still remember what it was like to be white.

chapters.title: The Fire That Never Dies
chapters.shortDesc: Argus stands on a ruined cathedral, uncertain whether he wants to extinguish the Light or punish it forever.
chapters.fullDesc:
"They call me the Dark Angel. I did not choose the name. I did not want it. But I have carried it for many years now, and I have learned that names are just words. What matters is what you do. And what I do is burn. That is enough."

Argus said that to a demon who asked why he still fought.

The night is dark over the Moniyan Empire, the stars hidden by clouds of ash and smoke. Argus stands on the ruins of a cathedral, his sword resting beside him, eyes fixed on the horizon.

The cathedral had once been beautiful: white towers, golden windows, bells that called the faithful to prayer. Now its roof is broken, its altar split, its statues blackened by fire. Green embers crawl along the cracks in the stone.

Somewhere out there, Rafaela is praying. Somewhere out there, the Church is rebuilding. Somewhere out there, the Light still shines.

Argus does not know if he will ever extinguish it. He does not know if he even wants to.

But he knows what he will do in the meantime.

He will fight. He will burn. He will never stop.

The blade waits. The fire burns. The darkness endures.

And as long as Argus draws breath, there will be someone reminding the world that the Light is not only mercy.

It is also judgment.

chapters.title: A Compendium of Argus's Powers and Techniques
chapters.shortDesc: A breakdown of Argus’s Abyssal rebirth, Demonic Blade, Meteoric Sword, Eternal Evil, and the aura of the Dark Angel.
chapters.fullDesc:
The Nature of His Power:
Argus's abilities are rooted in his transformation by the Abyss, a dark rebirth that turned him from an angel into a fallen. His power is not learned in the ordinary sense. It is given: curse and gift, wound and weapon.

The source of his strength is rage. He has turned pain into fury, grief into endurance, and rejection into a blade.

Demonic Blade:
Demonic Blade is Argus's signature technique, a charge that builds over time and drains life from enemies to sustain his own. He channels corrupted energy into the blade until its green flame intensifies. When he strikes, the weapon drinks.

Demonic Blade is not exhausting if he can keep feeding it, but each use deepens the corruption within him.

Meteoric Sword:
Meteoric Sword is Argus's mobility technique, a dash that lets him close distance quickly and strike before enemies can reposition. He launches forward with his blade extended, shadow wings trailing behind him like torn banners.

The technique drains stamina, but Argus can use it several times in battle if he conserves his strength.

Eternal Evil:
Eternal Evil is Argus's ultimate technique. For a short time, death cannot claim him. His life refuses to fall below its final point, and his attacks surge with Abyssal force.

The technique is devastating, but costly. Once it fades, Argus is left weakened and vulnerable.

The Aura of the Dark Angel:
Argus's passive aura is a constant cold pressure that settles on the skin of those near him. Allies feel protected and emboldened. Enemies feel doomed.

The aura is not something Argus controls. It is the darkness leaking from him like cold from ice. He cannot turn it off or direct it, but it has saved him many times by making enemies hesitate.

chapters.title: On the Dark Angel
chapters.shortDesc: The title is a burden and a gift. Argus carries it because someone must prove the Light can burn as well as heal.
chapters.fullDesc:
Dark Angel.

The title is a burden, but it is also a gift. It reminds Argus that he is not alone, that there are people who fear him, and that his actions matter. It reminds him of the mother he never knew. It reminds him of the sister he still loves. It reminds him of the Church that rejected him.

Argus does not know if he will ever be worthy of the title. He does not know if he will ever live up to the expectations that come with it.

But he knows that he will try.

He will try every day, in every battle, with every swing. He will be strong. He will be relentless. He will be immortal.

He will be the Dark Angel.

Not because he wants to be. Because he has to be.

Because someone has to remind the world that the Light can burn as well as heal.

And Argus, the twin born in shadow, the brother of the golden angel, the fallen who will never rise again, has decided that someone will be him.

The night is dark. The sword is ready. The fire burns.

And Argus never forgives.

chapters.title: The Steel That Refused to Be Ground Down
chapters.shortDesc: Fanny introduces herself as the Blade Dancer: a noble daughter who rejected tradition, forged her own cables, and claimed the sky.
chapters.fullDesc:
"They said a woman's place was in the parlor, not on the battlefield. They said I should paint flowers, not cut down enemies. They said the Wertz family's military legacy belonged to the men--my brother, my father, my uncles. I was supposed to be a decorator. A designer. A proper lady who managed the family business and bore children and never dreamed of anything more. They did not understand that the same blood that flowed through Tigreal's veins flowed through mine. The same steel that forged his shield forged my cables. The same fire that burned in his heart burned in mine. I did not ask for permission. I did not wait for approval. I forged my own weapons, taught myself to fly, and proved that the skies belong to anyone with the courage to reach for them. I am Fanny Wertz. I am the Blade Dancer. I am the sister of the empire's greatest defender, and I am his equal. The chains of tradition could not hold me. The ground could not contain me. I dance on the wind. And my enemies fall beneath my blades."

Fanny said those words to a young recruit who asked her how she learned to fly. She did not say them with pride exactly. Pride was too simple a word for what lived inside her. It was defiance, memory, pain, and freedom braided together like steel cable.

There is a particular kind of silence that falls over a training ground at dawn. It is not the silence of emptiness. The grounds of the Imperial Knights' Order are never truly empty, not with the clang of practice swords and the grunt of soldiers pushing their bodies to the limit. It is the silence of anticipation, of a world holding its breath, of a woman standing at the edge of a cliff with her steel cables coiled in her hands and her eyes fixed on the distant rooftops.

Fanny has known that silence since she was old enough to understand that the world did not expect her to be a warrior. She was born into the Wertz family, one of the most distinguished military lineages in the Moniyan Empire. The Wertz name meant honour, sacrifice, and service. For generations, the men of the family served in the Imperial Army, guarding the empire from its enemies, defending the weak, and upholding the law.

The women of the Wertz family were not soldiers. They were artists, designers, managers of the family's business affairs. They were expected to be graceful, cultured, and supportive--never on the front lines, never in danger, never holding a weapon.

Fanny was the youngest daughter, the baby of the family, the one who was supposed to be the most delicate, the most refined, the most proper. She was sent to art school. She learned to paint. She learned to design. She learned to smile and curtsy and say the right things at the right time.

She hated every moment of it.

Her brother Tigreal was her hero. He was everything she wanted to be: strong, brave, respected. He commanded armies. He protected the innocent. He made a difference. Fanny wanted to make a difference too.

When Tigreal was forced to leave home, taking the blame for a mistake in battle to protect his men, Fanny's resolve hardened. She would not wait. She would not ask permission. She would forge her own path.

She designed a weapon unlike any other: a pair of steel cables that could latch onto walls, cliffs, and rooftops, allowing her to swing through the air like a falcon hunting its prey. She trained in secret, falling, failing, rising again. She mastered the cables until they became an extension of her own body.

She joined the Imperial Knights' Order not as a man's daughter or a man's sister, but as Fanny Wertz: soldier, assassin, blade dancer. They called her the Blade of Freedom. They called her the Hovering Blade. They called her the terror of the battlefield.

She answered to none of them. She answered only to her own steel.

Her name is Fanny, and she is the Blade Dancer. This is her story: the story of a girl who refused to be confined by tradition, a woman who taught herself to fly, and a hero who proved that the sky is not a limit. It is a playground.

chapters.title: The Gilded Cage of Tradition
chapters.shortDesc: Castle Wertz raised boys to become soldiers and girls to become ornaments. Fanny rejected that cage before she was old enough to name it.
chapters.fullDesc:
Castle Wertz was not a fortress. It was a manor: a sprawling estate of manicured gardens, elegant ballrooms, and silent corridors lined with portraits of ancestors who had died for the empire. The Wertz family had wealth, influence, and a reputation for producing the finest soldiers in the Moniyan Army.

The men trained in the courtyard, their swords flashing, their voices raised in commands. The women watched from the balconies, their hands folded, their mouths silent.

Fanny Wertz was the youngest of five children, the only daughter, the one who was supposed to carry on the family's artistic legacy. Her mother had been a painter. Her grandmother had been a weaver. Her great-grandmother had designed the tapestries that hung in the Imperial Palace.

"You have the gift," her mother said, placing a paintbrush in Fanny's tiny fingers. "You will create beauty, not destroy it."

Fanny looked at the paintbrush. She looked at her brother Tigreal, who was sparring in the courtyard, his shield raised, his sword singing. Then she dropped the brush.

"I want to fight," she said.

Her mother laughed. It was a gentle laugh, but it carried the weight of centuries.

"Girls do not fight, Fanny. Girls create. Girls nurture. Girls support. The men protect us. That is the way of things."

Fanny did not accept that way. She never would. Even as a child, she understood that a cage did not become kinder because it was gilded, and a command did not become truth because it had been repeated for generations.

She learned her lessons because she had to. She painted flowers, stitched hems, memorised etiquette, and smiled when visitors praised her refinement. But when she looked out the window and saw the men training, her fingers twitched for a sword instead of a brush.

The world had chosen a shape for her. Fanny had already begun sharpening herself against it.

chapters.title: The Hero in the Shining Armor
chapters.shortDesc: Tigreal was Fanny’s hero and first teacher. In secret, he treated her like a recruit and taught her not to let anyone extinguish her fire.
chapters.fullDesc:
Tigreal was ten years older than Fanny, already a man when she was still a child. He was everything a Wertz was supposed to be: tall, strong, honourable, brave. He had joined the Imperial Knights' Order at sixteen, risen through the ranks, and earned a reputation as the empire's most promising young commander.

To Fanny, he was not just a brother. He was a god.

Whenever Tigreal returned to Castle Wertz on leave, Fanny abandoned her lessons, slipped away from her tutors, and found him. He told her stories of the battlefield, not the sanitised versions the bards sang, but the real ones: the fear, the blood, the moments when death brushed past his cheek and he knew he was alive.

"Don't tell Mother," he would say after describing a particularly gruesome battle.

"I won't," Fanny promised.

She never did.

Tigreal taught her to fight in secret. He showed her how to hold a sword, how to balance her weight, how to strike and retreat. He did not coddle her. He treated her as he would treat any recruit: with respect, with rigour, with the expectation that she would rise to the challenge.

"You have the fire," he told her. "The same fire that burns in me. Do not let anyone extinguish it."

Fanny clutched those words like a talisman. She repeated them when her tutors corrected her posture. She repeated them when her mother scolded the calluses forming on her palms. She repeated them at night, alone in her room, moving through sword forms in the dark where no one could see.

She would need those words in the years to come. They became the first cable she ever trusted: invisible, unbreakable, stretching between the girl she was and the warrior she intended to become.

chapters.title: The Promise That Was Broken
chapters.shortDesc: Tigreal promised to help Fanny enter military life when she came of age. When disgrace forced him away, she stopped waiting.
chapters.fullDesc:
When Fanny was fourteen, Tigreal made her a promise.

"When you turn eighteen, I will take you to the Light's Order headquarters. I will show you what it means to be a soldier. And if you still want to join after that--if you still have the fire--I will help you."

Fanny was ecstatic. Four years. She could wait four years. She would train in secret, prepare herself, and prove that she was worthy.

But Tigreal did not make it to her eighteenth birthday.

A battle went wrong: a betrayal, a trap, a mistake that was not his fault but that he chose to carry anyway. He took the blame to protect his men, shielding them from political fallout that would have destroyed their careers.

He left the capital. He left the army. He left Fanny.

The household whispered. Some called him noble. Some called him foolish. Some called him disgraced. Fanny listened to all of them and said nothing. The brother who had promised to open the gate for her was gone, and the adults around her seemed to think that meant the gate had closed forever.

They did not understand her at all.

The day she heard the news, Fanny did not cry. She walked to the training yard, picked up a practice sword, and swung it until her hands bled. Each strike was a refusal. Each breath was a decision.

She had waited long enough. She would not wait any longer. If no one would open the path for her, she would carve one through steel, stone, and sky.

chapters.title: The Steel Cable That Changed Everything
chapters.shortDesc: A dream of flight became an invention. Fanny built her own grappling cables through failure, bruises, obsession, and stubborn genius.
chapters.fullDesc:
The idea came to her in a dream.

She was flying, soaring above the mountains, the wind in her hair and the clouds beneath her feet. She felt free, weightless, unstoppable. When she woke, the dream was over, but the feeling lingered.

Fanny realised she would never be a traditional soldier. She was too small, too light, too different from the men who filled the army's ranks. She could not match their strength, endurance, or brute force.

But she could be faster. She could be smarter. She could be everywhere at once.

So she began to design the cables.

The first prototypes were failures. The steel was too weak, the hooks were too blunt, the mechanisms too slow. She spent months in the family's workshop, salvaging materials, testing designs, and cursing her failures. Her hands turned black with grease. Her notebooks filled with diagrams. Her sleep became a luxury she could not afford.

Her family thought she had lost her mind. They did not understand why the youngest daughter spent her days surrounded by scrap metal and calculations, eyes wild with obsession.

"She is wasting her talent," her mother said.

"She is finding herself," a servant whispered.

The servant was right.

After a year of trial and error, Fanny completed her masterpiece: a pair of lightweight but strong steel cables, tipped with retractable grappling hooks that could latch onto stone, wood, and metal. The cables attached to a harness around her waist, controlled through subtle shifts of her body.

She tested them on the cliffs behind Castle Wertz. The first attempts ended in bruises, scrapes, and terrifying falls. She misjudged angles. She slammed into stone. She dangled helplessly from ledges while servants screamed below.

But she did not stop. She kept climbing, kept falling, kept learning.

Eventually, she flew.

chapters.title: The Imperial Knights' Order and the Walls of Prejudice
chapters.shortDesc: Fanny enlisted without leaning on the Wertz name. The Order laughed at her cables until she crossed the room faster than doubt could follow.
chapters.fullDesc:
Fanny enlisted in the Imperial Knights' Order three days after her eighteenth birthday.

She did not use her family name. She did not mention her brother. She presented herself as Fanny, a young woman with a strange weapon and an unshakeable determination.

The recruiting officer laughed when he saw her cables.

"What are those supposed to be? A child's toy?"

"They are my weapons," Fanny replied. "And they will make me the best soldier you have ever seen."

The officer stopped laughing when she demonstrated her abilities. She flew across the training ground, swinging from the rafters, landing behind him before he could turn around. Her twin blades flashed, and a practice dummy fell apart in three pieces.

"Where did you learn to do that?" he asked, his voice suddenly quiet.

"I taught myself," she said.

She was accepted into the Order.

The other recruits were not welcoming. They whispered about the girl with the cables, the Wertz family's disappointment, the sister of the disgraced commander. They watched her like a curiosity, then like a threat.

Fanny did not care. She trained harder than anyone else. She rose earlier, stayed later, and pushed her body until exhaustion became background noise. She learned to read the battlefield, anticipate enemy movements, and strike from angles no one expected.

Within a year, she had earned her place. Within two, she had earned her reputation.

They called her the Blade Dancer because when she fought, she did not fight. She danced: a deadly, beautiful, impossible dance that left her enemies wondering where she had gone, why they were bleeding, and how she had already moved on.

chapters.title: The Blade of Freedom
chapters.shortDesc: On her first major mission, Fanny proved she was not merely a scout. She was a weapon the battlefield had never seen before.
chapters.fullDesc:
Fanny's first major mission was a counter-assassination operation in the lawless territories of Los Pecados.

A rogue noble had hired mercenaries to eliminate a rival. The Imperial Knights' Order was tasked with intercepting them before they could strike. Fanny was assigned as a scout because her cables made her ideal for reconnaissance, moving ahead of the main force and reporting enemy positions.

She did more than scout.

She found the mercenaries' camp, counted their numbers, and mapped their defences. Then she returned to her commander and requested permission to engage.

"There are fifty of them and one of you," the commander said.

"I know," Fanny replied. "I also know they are sleeping. They do not expect an attack. They do not expect me."

The commander hesitated. Then he nodded.

"Show me what you can do."

Fanny flew into the camp.

The mercenaries woke to the sound of screaming. By the time the main force arrived, half the camp was dead, and the rest were fleeing into the night. Fanny stood in the centre of the carnage, blades dripping, cables coiled at her hips.

The commander looked at her with something like awe.

"You are not a scout," he said. "You are a weapon."

Fanny smiled. It was not a warm smile.

"I know."

Word of the mission travelled quickly. Some praised her. Some feared her. Some argued that no soldier should move like that, strike like that, vanish like that. Fanny ignored them all. The sky had opened above her, and for the first time in her life, the world below seemed small enough to conquer.

chapters.title: The Form of the Skyborne Warrior
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed portrait of Fanny: lean, hawk-eyed, golden-haired, clad in purple and gold, with Twin Fangs and cable mechanisms at her hips.
chapters.fullDesc:
To look at Fanny is to see a contradiction given flesh.

She is small: shorter than most soldiers, lighter than most recruits. Her physique is not bulky. It is lean, coiled, built for speed and agility rather than brute force. Her muscles are dense, her reflexes sharp, her body a finely tuned instrument of motion.

Her face is the face of a woman who has never taken no for an answer. Her jawline is sharp and regal, the kind of bone structure artists love to sketch and enemies learn to fear. Her cheekbones are high, casting shadows that make her eyes seem even deeper than they already are. Her nose is straight and noble, perfectly proportioned to the rest of her features. Her skin is fair, almost porcelain, with a subtle golden undertone.

Her eyes are her most striking feature. They are large, expressive, a piercing shade of blue-violet that seems to shift with her mood. They are the eyes of a hawk: constantly scanning, constantly calculating, constantly ready.

Her hair is a vibrant mane of golden yellow, a dynamic cascade that mirrors her relentless energy. Thick, jagged bangs frame her forehead and temples, while the rest is pulled back into a high, spiky ponytail that flares upward like a flame caught in perpetual motion.

Her upper body is clad in a skin-tight one-piece combat suit in deep regal purple, textured with vertical ribbing for maximum flexibility. Over it she wears ornate armour of polished silver and gold: a gold-trimmed collar rising behind her neck, a stylised metallic belt at her waist, and a diamond-shaped silver buckle.

Her forearms are encased in bulky purple gauntlets reinforced with silver plating and gold accents at the wrists, armour designed not merely for protection but to withstand the tremendous forces of her grappling cables. Her lower legs are shielded by sophisticated greaves that begin at the knees with sharp golden wing-like protrusions, tapering into sleek dark boots.

At her hips sit her most distinctive equipment: two heavy gear mechanisms, one on each side. They are scabbards for her twin blades, but more than that, they are the heart of her mobility, housing high-tension steel cables and grappling hooks that she can fire with a thought.

Her weapons are a pair of twin short swords forged from brilliant silver metal. Sleek, balanced, and designed for speed, their wide flat fullers catch the light as they move. Intricate crossguards set with circular blue gems pulse faintly.

The blades are named the Twin Fangs. They have killed more enemies than Fanny can count.

chapters.title: Steel Cable - The Thread That Connects Earth to Sky
chapters.shortDesc: Fanny’s signature technique is not magic. It is engineering, trust, timing, and the courage to fall until flight becomes instinct.
chapters.fullDesc:
Steel Cable is Fanny's signature technique: the ability that defines her, makes her unique, and allows her to dance where others can only walk.

The cables are not magical. They are not blessed. They are simply tools: well-designed, well-crafted, and well-maintained. Fanny fires a cable toward a wall, cliff, or rooftop. The grappling hook latches onto the surface, and the cable retracts, pulling her through the air.

She can chain these movements together, swinging from one anchor point to the next, building momentum and accelerating until she becomes a blur of purple and gold against the sky.

The technique requires years of practice. The timing must be perfect. The angle must be precise. The energy must be managed. Fanny has spent more hours training with the cables than she has spent sleeping.

"It is not about strength," she tells young soldiers who ask how she does it. "It is about trust. Trust in the cables. Trust in your body. Trust that you will not fall."

She has fallen many times. She has the scars to prove it. Some are thin white lines across her ribs. Some are old bruises buried deep in her joints. Some are memories of impact: stone rushing up, breath leaving her lungs, the taste of blood in her mouth.

But she has never stopped getting up.

To Fanny, flight is not escape. It is discipline. It is precision. It is the moment when fear becomes calculation and calculation becomes motion. The cable fires. The hook catches. The world falls away.

Then the Blade Dancer moves.

chapters.title: Tornado Strike and Cut Throat - The Dance of Death
chapters.shortDesc: Tornado Strike marks the prey. Cut Throat ends the hunt. Together, they turn Fanny’s flight into execution.
chapters.fullDesc:
Tornado Strike is Fanny's area-control technique, a spinning slash unleashed as she flies through an enemy, damaging them and marking them as prey.

The technique is simple but devastating. Fanny swings her blades as she passes, twin arcs of silver cutting through armour, flesh, and bone. The motion is fluid, almost graceful: the dance of a predator who has perfected her kill.

Tornado Strike is not exhausting. Fanny can use it as often as she flies through enemies, as long as she has the energy to swing. But each strike leaves her momentarily vulnerable, and she must manage her momentum carefully. A missed angle can turn a beautiful attack into a fatal mistake.

Cut Throat is Fanny's ultimate technique, a devastating lunge delivered to a marked enemy for massive burst damage.

It is the culmination of everything Fanny is: hunter, predator, dancer of death. She locks onto her target, fires her cables, and launches herself forward like an arrow from a bow. Her blades find the enemy's heart, and the battle ends.

Cut Throat is exhausting. Each use drains Fanny's energy reserves, and the close range leaves her vulnerable for a heartbeat afterward. She uses it sparingly, saving it for moments when an enemy is isolated, wounded, or unable to escape.

But when she uses it, she uses it with all the fury in her steel-hardened heart.

Enemies who survive seeing Tornado Strike learn to fear the mark it leaves behind. Enemies who see Cut Throat rarely survive long enough to learn anything at all.

chapters.title: The Lightborn and the Sister's Shadow
chapters.shortDesc: Silvanna recruited Fanny into the Lightborn, where she fought beside Tigreal and proved she was not his shadow but his equal.
chapters.fullDesc:
Fanny was recruited into the Lightborn squad by Silvanna herself.

The Lightborn was an elite unit formed to combat the growing threat of the Abyss. Its members were the empire's finest: Silvanna, Tigreal, Alucard, Harith, Granger. Fanny was honoured to be included, but she knew her brother's shadow would follow her.

Tigreal had been the empire's greatest defender. Fanny was his sister. The comparisons were inevitable.

"You fight like him," Silvanna observed after watching Fanny train.

"I fight like myself," Fanny replied.

"You use the same techniques. The same strategies. The same fury."

"He taught me. But I made them my own."

Silvanna nodded. She understood.

Fanny earned her place in the Lightborn. She fought beside her brother not as his inferior, but as his equal. Together, they pushed back Abyssal forces, defended the empire's borders, and saved countless lives.

The whispers did not stop entirely. But they grew quieter.

Fanny did not need silence. She needed action. Every battle gave her another chance to prove what she had known since childhood: that courage was not inherited through sons alone, that steel did not care about tradition, and that the sky belonged to the one brave enough to claim it.

chapters.title: The Sister's Reunion
chapters.shortDesc: The Lightborn brought Fanny and Tigreal together again. They did not need speeches; their blades and shields remembered each other.
chapters.fullDesc:
Fanny and Tigreal had not spoken in years.

The distance had not been angry. It had simply been distance. Tigreal had left to protect his men. Fanny had stayed to forge her own path. They had both been busy, both proud, both too stubborn to reach out.

The Lightborn brought them together.

The first time Fanny saw her brother on the battlefield, her heart clenched. He was older now, greyer, wearier. The weight of command had carved lines into his face that had not been there before.

"Brother," she said.

"Sister," he replied.

They did not embrace. They did not weep. They simply stood there, two warriors shaped by the same fire and tempered by the same steel.

"You have done well," Tigreal said.

"I learned from the best," Fanny replied.

They fought side by side that day. They did not need to speak. They knew each other's movements, rhythms, and thoughts. Tigreal raised his shield before Fanny needed cover. Fanny cut down enemies before they reached his blind side. Every motion was memory.

They were Wertz. They were warriors. They were family.

By sunset, the field was quiet. Tigreal looked at the cables at her hips, the blood on her blades, the calm in her eyes.

"You fly well," he said.

Fanny smiled.

"I know."

chapters.title: The Legacy of the Blade Dancer
chapters.shortDesc: Fanny does not know if the Abyss will fall or if the empire will accept her. She only knows that she will keep flying.
chapters.fullDesc:
Fanny does not know what the future holds.

She does not know if the Abyss will ever be defeated. She does not know if the empire will ever fully accept her. She does not know if the cables will ever fail.

But she knows what she will do in the meantime.

She will fly. She will fight. She will dance.

The cables never break. The blades never dull. The dancer never stops.

She is Fanny, the Blade Dancer, and she will never stop proving that the sky belongs to anyone with the courage to reach for it.

Her legacy is not a statue or a song. It is the sound of steel cable firing into stone. It is the blur of purple and gold over a battlefield. It is the startled silence of enemies who thought they understood the limits of war and then looked up.

It is every girl who watches Fanny fly and realises that a cage is only permanent if no one teaches you how to break it.

The Wertz family wanted her to create beauty. In a way, she did. Her beauty is motion. Her canvas is the sky. Her brush is a blade.

chapters.title: The Dance That Never Ends
chapters.shortDesc: On a rooftop above the capital, Fanny keeps watch. The city sleeps below; the Blade Dancer remains ready above.
chapters.fullDesc:
"They call me the Blade Dancer. I did not choose the name. I do not care about names. I care about the flight. The freedom. The moment when I am suspended between earth and sky, and nothing else matters. I am Fanny. I am the dancer in the wind. I am the terror of the battlefield. And I will never stop moving."

Fanny said that to a young recruit who asked why she never stands still.

The night is dark over the Moniyan Empire, the stars bright enough to see through the thin veil of clouds. Fanny stands on a rooftop overlooking the capital, cables coiled at her hips, eyes fixed on the horizon.

The city is quiet. The people are sleeping. The threats are distant.

But Fanny does not sleep. She watches. She waits. She is always ready.

She thinks about her brother, who taught her to fight. She thinks about her mother, who wanted her to paint. She thinks about the cables, which she designed with her own hands. She does not hate the life that was offered to her. Hatred would be too easy. She simply knows it was never hers.

She does not know if she will ever find peace. She does not know if the world will ever be truly safe. She does not know if the dance will ever end.

But she knows what she will do in the meantime.

She will fly. She will fight. She will dance.

The cables wait. The blades are sharp. The dancer is ready. And as long as Fanny draws breath, there will be someone watching over the empire from the skies.

chapters.title: A Compendium of Fanny's Powers and Techniques
chapters.shortDesc: A full breakdown of Fanny’s mechanical mobility, Air Superiority, Steel Cable, Tornado Strike, Cut Throat, and battlefield aura.
chapters.fullDesc:
The Nature of Her Power:
Fanny's abilities are not magical. They are mechanical: the product of her ingenuity, determination, and refusal to accept limitations. The steel cables are her invention, her signature, and her soul.

The source of her power is will. She has trained her body to move faster than thought, to react before she has consciously decided to react, and to trust her instincts absolutely.

Her blades are extensions of that will: weapons that respond to her touch, sing as they cut through the air, and carry the weight of her determination.

Air Superiority:
Fanny's passive ability enhances her damage and restores her energy when she attacks while flying. It is automatic, a natural consequence of her mobility. She does not need to activate it. It simply happens whenever she is in motion.

Steel Cable:
Fanny's signature technique allows her to fire a grappling hook at a wall, cliff, or rooftop, pulling herself toward it at incredible speed. The technique requires precise aim and careful energy management. Each cable costs energy, though chained cables become easier as momentum builds.

Steel Cable is not exhausting if she manages it well. Fanny can use it as often as she has the energy to fire. But each hook leaves her vulnerable, and she must maintain momentum to avoid becoming a stationary target.

Tornado Strike:
Tornado Strike is a spinning slash unleashed when Fanny flies through an enemy, damaging them and marking them as prey. The technique is simple but devastating, a natural consequence of her flight.

Cut Throat:
Cut Throat is Fanny's ultimate technique: a devastating lunge delivered to a marked enemy for massive burst damage. She locks onto her target, fires her cables, and launches herself forward like an arrow from a bow.

Cut Throat is exhausting. Each use drains her energy reserves, leaving her weak and vulnerable for a moment afterward. She reserves it for enemies who are isolated, wounded, or unable to escape.

The Aura of the Blade Dancer:
Fanny's passive aura is a constant presence, a tension that settles on the skin of those near her. Allies feel energised, ready to fight. Enemies feel watched, hunted.

The aura is not something Fanny controls. It is a natural byproduct of her mobility, the anticipation of her movement leaking from her like heat from an engine. She cannot turn it off, direct it, or use it as a weapon.

But she is grateful for it. The aura has saved her life many times, not by healing wounds, but by making enemies hesitate, doubt, and fear.

chapters.title: On the Blade Dancer
chapters.shortDesc: The title is a burden and a gift. Fanny carries it because someone must watch the skies, and she has chosen herself.
chapters.fullDesc:
Blade Dancer.

The title is a burden, but it is also a gift. It reminds Fanny that she is not alone, that there are people who depend on her, and that her actions matter. It reminds her of the brother who taught her to fight. It reminds her of the mother who wanted her to paint. It reminds her of the cables she designed with her own hands.

Fanny does not know if she will ever be worthy of the title. She does not know if she will ever live up to the expectations that come with it.

But she knows that she will try.

She will try every day, in every battle, with every swing. She will be fast. She will be fearless. She will be free.

She will be the Blade Dancer.

Not because she wants to be. Because she has to be.

Because someone has to watch the skies.

And Fanny, the youngest daughter of the Wertz family, the sister of Tigreal, the inventor of the steel cables, has decided that someone will be her.

The night is dark. The cables are ready. The dance is waiting.

And Fanny never stops flying.

chapters.title: The Tempest That Refuses to Be Caged
chapters.shortDesc: Ling speaks as the Cyan Finch: once a disciple of the Great Dragon, now a phantom assassin still haunted by Zilong’s selection.
chapters.fullDesc:
"They say I am a ghost. A phantom that haunts the peaks of the Cadia Riverlands, a swordsman whose blade is like a tempest and whose whereabouts are impossible to predict. They are not wrong. I am Ling, the Cyan Finch. I was once a disciple of the Great Dragon, one of two prodigies destined to inherit the power of the Celestial Guardians. I trained alongside Zilong, my friend, my rival, my brother in arms. We pushed each other to be faster, stronger, sharper. We dreamed of standing together at the pinnacle of martial perfection. But the Great Dragon saw something in him that he did not see in me."

Ling said those words to a young assassin who asked why he never spoke of the past. He did not answer with rage. Rage would have been too simple. His voice carried something colder: remembrance sharpened until it became a blade.

There is a particular silence that falls over the Sky Arch when the clouds part. It is not emptiness. The peaks are alive with wind, distant eagles, and the soft scrape of frost against stone. It is the silence of a world holding its breath before a swordsman returns to the threshold of a place that once called him disciple.

Ling was not always the Cyan Finch. Once he was a kind-hearted but guarded swordsman, a prodigy taken in by the Great Dragon and trained in the sacred arts of the Hidden Land. He lived beside Zilong, the Spear of the Dragon, and together they were the brightest stars of their generation.

They trained together, sparred together, dreamed together. Zilong was steady, loyal, and humble. Ling was faster, sharper, hungrier. Each believed he might one day inherit the Dragon's legacy.

The Great Dragon chose Zilong.

Ling left with nothing but his sword and wounded pride. He wandered the Cadia Riverlands until he found the Finch, a secret order of assassins dressed in black with cyan embroidery. They gave him a new name, a new purpose, and a family made of outcasts.

Now Ling moves like wind across rooftops, cliffs, and clouded peaks. His sword is a tempest. His footsteps are impossible to follow. Yet every path still bends toward one unfinished question.

Was the Great Dragon right?

Ling will not stop until he has forced the answer from Zilong's blade.

chapters.title: The Hidden Land of the Dragon
chapters.shortDesc: Ling arrives at the Sky Arch as a gifted orphan and enters the Great Dragon’s brutal sanctuary of Qinggong and sword discipline.
chapters.fullDesc:
At the top of mountains veiled by cloud lay the entrance to the Hidden Land of the Dragon, a place called the Sky Arch. Beyond it stretched ancient temples, misty peaks, suspended bridges, and training courtyards carved into stone older than memory. The air was thin, the cold was biting, and the path was treacherous. Only the worthy could find their way. Only the dedicated could stay.

Ling arrived as a boy, thin-bodied and wide-eyed, with no family to claim him. Scouts of the Great Dragon had found him in the Cadia Riverlands, a child with unnatural speed and instinctive swordsmanship. He moved like a frightened bird, always ready to flee, yet his gaze stayed fixed on every blade he saw.

The Great Dragon offered him a place to belong. The ancient guardian appeared in human form when speaking to children: tall, grave, and robed in pale jade and gold, with eyes that held the weight of storms.

"You will train with the others," the Great Dragon said. "You will learn the way of the blade, the art of lightness, and the discipline of the warrior. If you prove worthy, you may one day stand beside me as successor."

Ling accepted without hesitation. He had nothing else.

The Hidden Land was a crucible. Masters demanded balance on bamboo tips, leaps between cliffs, stillness under falling snow, and sword forms repeated until muscles trembled. Ling threw himself into the work with ferocity. He learned to run along lake water without breaking its skin, cross chasms with a single breath, and dance across high walls like a bird on the wind.

He was not alone. Another disciple, Zilong, had been taken in as a foundling too. Zilong was quieter, steadier, and more patient. He did not have Ling's explosive talent, but he carried something the Great Dragon valued above all else.

"Loyalty," the Great Dragon said, watching Zilong train. "He has the heart of a guardian. He fights not for himself, but for others."

Ling did not understand. Was the desire to be the best not enough?

He would learn the answer, but not yet.

chapters.title: The Rival and the Friend
chapters.shortDesc: Ling and Zilong become rivals, brothers in training, and mirrors of two different philosophies of strength.
chapters.fullDesc:
Ling and Zilong became rivals almost immediately.

They were the two strongest disciples, the ones most likely to be chosen as the Great Dragon's successor. They sparred constantly, blade against spear, speed against patience. Ling moved like a flash of cyan across the courtyard. Zilong held his ground with calm precision, his spear drawing circles of disciplined force.

"You are faster," Zilong admitted after one brutal session.

"You are stronger," Ling replied.

"Speed is not everything. Strength is not everything. The Great Dragon says the greatest warrior fights for something greater than himself."

Ling laughed. "I fight for myself. That is enough."

Zilong did not argue. He simply nodded, as if he understood something Ling did not.

Despite their rivalry, they became friends. They trained together, ate together, and slept in the same dormitory beneath paper lanterns and carved dragon beams. They shared stories of their pasts. Zilong spoke of his father, a travelling craftsman lost to the river. Ling spoke of nothing. He had no past to share. The Great Dragon had given him everything he could remember worth keeping.

"You are lucky," Zilong said. "You have no memories to haunt you."

"I am not lucky," Ling replied. "I am empty. I am trying to fill the emptiness with skill, power, and the hope that one day I will be chosen."

"Being chosen is not the goal," Zilong said. "Being worthy is."

Ling did not understand. But he remembered the words.

Years later, after the choice broke him, those words would return like a blade in the dark.

chapters.title: The Choice That Broke Him
chapters.shortDesc: At the Dragon Altar, the Great Dragon chooses Zilong. Ling leaves the Hidden Land without goodbye.
chapters.fullDesc:
The day of the Great Dragon's choice arrived without warning.

He called Ling and Zilong to the Dragon Altar, the sacred platform at the heart of the Hidden Land. The altar stood above a sea of cloud, ringed by stone pillars carved with celestial guardians. Other disciples gathered in silence, their eyes bright with anticipation.

The Great Dragon looked at both young men. He spoke of their strengths, weaknesses, and potential. He praised Ling's speed, precision, mastery of Qinggong, and sword talent. Then he praised Zilong's loyalty, humility, discipline, and willingness to sacrifice.

Then he made his choice.

"Zilong will be my successor. He will inherit the legacy of the Dragon. He will be my adopted son."

Ling felt the world tilt beneath him.

He had worked so hard. He had sacrificed youth, comfort, sleep, and tenderness. He had been faster, sharper, more skilled in every measurable way.

And still, he had lost.

"Why?" he asked, voice trembling. "Why him and not me?"

"Because he fights for something greater than himself," the Great Dragon said. "You fight for yourself. That is the difference."

Ling could not accept it. The words felt like dismissal wrapped in wisdom, rejection disguised as instruction. He saw pity in the eyes of other disciples. Worse, he imagined pity in Zilong's.

He stormed out of the Dragon Altar, fists clenched, tears burning but unshed. That night he packed his belongings and left the Hidden Land.

He did not say goodbye to Zilong.

He could not bear to see his face.

chapters.title: The Anatomy of a Tempestuous Blade
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed portrait of Ling: violet hair and eyes, teal forehead mark, blue feathered finery, and the glowing Tempest Blade.
chapters.fullDesc:
To look at Ling is to see a paradox of grace and violence.

He stands just over five and a half feet tall, with a physique that balances the lithe elegance of a dancer and the coiled power of a predator. He is not bulky. Ling relies on speed and agility, but his body is dense with the muscle earned from years of leaping, climbing, and wielding a blade as if it were part of his soul.

His face is the face of a man who learned to trust only his sword. His jawline is sharp and aristocratic, softened by a hidden sensitivity he rarely allows anyone to see. His cheekbones are high, his nose straight and slender, his skin fair with a faint golden undertone.

His eyes are deep soulful violet, matching his hair, calm at first glance but piercing when focused. A teal diamond mark rests vertically at the centre of his forehead, a sign of his connection to the Vermilion Bird, celestial guardian of the South.

His hair is light violet, styled in a sophisticated chin-length bob with asymmetrical bangs sweeping across his forehead and framing his eyes. It gives him an ethereal elegance that contrasts with the lethal certainty of his movements.

His upper body is dressed in a high-collared, form-fitting tunic of deep royal blue, embroidered with gold filigree and emerald accents like iridescent plumage. The collar rises behind his neck like a fan of feathers. Elegant golden pauldrons curve upward from his shoulders.

His sleeves widen into layered bell-shaped cuffs at the wrists, dark blue and turquoise feathers creating a wing-like effect whenever he moves. A long tailcoat flows from his back, split into feathery fronds of cerulean and peacock-eye patterns.

His black trousers fit close to long slender legs, tucked into polished black boots with gold trim.

His weapon is a long slender blade, more stylised feather or crystalline shard than ordinary sword. It glows teal-green, tapering to a needle point, with golden filigree at the handle and a sapphire peacock-eye gem at the pommel.

The blade is named the Tempest Blade.

It has drawn more blood than Ling can count.

chapters.title: The Loner's Path
chapters.shortDesc: After exile, Ling trains alone on cliffs and cloud lakes until loneliness drives him toward the shadows.
chapters.fullDesc:
After leaving the Hidden Land, Ling wandered the edges of the Cadia Riverlands.

He had no destination, no purpose, and no reason to live except his sword. He slept in caves, ate what he could hunt, and trained every waking hour. He practised Qinggong on sheer cliffs while wind tried to tear him loose. He repeated sword forms in storms until rain blurred the world into silver lines.

The loneliness was crushing. There was no one to spar with, no one to correct his stance, no one to share his burdens. He thought about Zilong, the Great Dragon, and the life he had left behind. He wondered if he had made a mistake. He wondered if he would ever be happy again.

He found no answers. Only more questions.

But he also found clarity.

The Great Dragon had not rejected him because he was weak. Ling knew that. He had rejected him because Ling was different: because he fought for himself, because he had no one else to fight for, because the hunger inside him frightened those who mistook hunger for selfishness.

So Ling decided to find someone.

Not a master. Not a friend like Zilong had been. A family. A group of outcasts who had also been rejected by the world. People who understood what it meant to be useful, feared, and unwanted.

He found them in the shadows.

chapters.title: The Birth of the Finch
chapters.shortDesc: Ling challenges the Finch assassins, wins their respect, and becomes the Cyan Finch: their sharpest claw.
chapters.fullDesc:
The Finch was a secret organisation: a network of assassins dressed in black, their cyan embroidery marking them as members of the most mysterious faction in the Cadia Riverlands.

They were outcasts, criminals, rebels, and survivors. Some had been cast out by noble clans. Some had fled corrupt magistrates. Some had chosen blood over poverty and never looked back. They were feared, respected, and utterly ruthless.

Their garments were dark and practical, with masks that left only the eyes visible. Cyan thread marked cuffs, collars, and sashes in patterns resembling feathers. Each assassin carried curved knives, hidden darts, and climbing hooks, but none moved like Ling.

Ling sought them out. He challenged their leader to single combat and won. The duel took place under a moonless sky on a roof slick with rain. The Finch leader was fast, but Ling was faster. When the Tempest Blade stopped at the leader's throat, the watching assassins did not cheer. They bowed.

"Legends say it is impossible to escape the claws of the Finch," they whispered. "Now we have a new claw. The Cyan Finch. The best among us."

Ling trained with them, fought with them, and bled with them. He learned their techniques, strategies, code, and silence. He became their greatest assassin, a phantom who appeared from nowhere and vanished before the blood hit the ground.

But he never forgot his true purpose. He was not only an assassin. He was a swordsman with a score to settle.

"The Cyan Finch cannot tolerate failure," he told himself.

This time would be no different.

chapters.title: The Raid on the Hidden Land
chapters.shortDesc: Ling leads the Finch through the Sky Arch, but the Hidden Land’s traps swallow his assassins and leave him to enter alone.
chapters.fullDesc:
The opportunity came years later.

Ling had gathered enough intelligence, allies, and power to attempt what he had always dreamed of: a raid on the Hidden Land of the Dragon.

He led his assassins to the Sky Arch, entrance to the Great Dragon's domain. Mist churned beneath them like a lake without water. With his lithe footwork, Ling crossed the cloud surface without creating a ripple. He drew his blade, swung once, and generated enough energy to open the Sky Arch.

The assassins behind him dashed forward.

The Hidden Land was not defenceless. Occult traps and enchantments had guarded it for centuries. The Finch were skilled, but they were intruders in a realm shaped by the Great Dragon's will. Their hooks failed. Their steps faltered. Some lost their balance and fell into the white abyss below, bodies swallowed by mist before they could scream.

Ling did not fall.

His light feet glided over every peril, past every enchantment. He moved across walls, branches, roofs, and floating stones as if the Hidden Land itself remembered him too late.

He reached the Great Dragon Palace while guards were distracted by turmoil at the Sky Arch. The palace stood empty and luminous, jade tiles reflecting cold moonlight, dragon banners shifting in the wind.

Ling stood on a high point overlooking the place where he had once been called disciple.

He had come for one thing: to face Zilong. To prove he was the better warrior. To settle the score once and for all.

But Zilong was not there.

chapters.title: The Tempest of Blades
chapters.shortDesc: Denied his rival, Ling unleashes Tempest of Blades in an empty palace and discovers that rage without an opponent is only echo.
chapters.fullDesc:
Instead of Zilong, Ling found an empty throne, a silent hall, and the lingering presence of the Great Dragon's power.

He had come so far. He had sacrificed followers, years, tenderness, and sleep. He had sharpened himself into a weapon for this moment.

His rival was nowhere to be found.

Rage erupted.

Ling swung the Tempest Blade and unleashed his ultimate technique. Four swords answered, forming a field of cutting energy around him. The air screamed. Teal light flashed across pillars and polished floors. Within the field, Ling moved between blades like an untargetable phantom, appearing and vanishing faster than sight could follow.

The palace shook.

But there was no one to fight. No one to defeat. No one to force into acknowledgement.

The summoned swords faded one by one. Silence returned, heavier than before.

Ling sheathed his blade. His face remained calm, but his hand trembled against the hilt.

He turned and left the palace as silently as he had entered.

He had not found what he was looking for. But he had found something else: a clearer purpose. He would continue to search. He would continue to train. He would wait for the day he could finally face Zilong and end their rivalry.

"I am the Cyan Finch," he whispered as he disappeared into the mist. "I cannot tolerate failure."

chapters.title: The Master of Qinggong and Swordplay
chapters.shortDesc: Ling’s abilities combine wall-running Qinggong, Finch Poise, Defiant Sword, and the terrifying Tempest of Blades.
chapters.fullDesc:
Ling's abilities are legendary.

He is a master of Qinggong, the ancient art of lightness that allows him to leap among walls, run across water, and glide through the air like a bird. His Cloud Walker discipline lets him remain above the battlefield, gathering Lightness as long as he moves from wall to wall.

Finch Poise is the foundation of his mobility. With it, Ling leaps onto walls, perches where ordinary warriors cannot stand, and shifts from surface to surface with impossible speed. From above, he watches battlefields like a hawk studying prey.

Defiant Sword is his primary strike. It is a precise, powerful slash that pierces enemy defence, slows movement, and feeds him through lifesteal when used with perfect timing. From a wall, it becomes even more dangerous: a falling cut of teal light and surgical violence.

Tempest of Blades is his ultimate expression. Four swords descend around him, forming a field of lethal energy. Within it, Ling can move between blades, briefly becoming untouchable as he repositions, evades, and kills.

"How do you like this move?" Ling sometimes sneers as the blades spin.

He is among the most agile warriors in the Land of Dawn: a phantom who can strike from any angle and vanish before enemies understand where he stood.

He is the Cyan Finch.

He has never been caught.

chapters.title: The Vermilion Bird's Legacy
chapters.shortDesc: Ling represents the Vermilion Bird among the Oriental Fighters, fighting beside Zilong, Baxia, and Wanwan despite old wounds.
chapters.fullDesc:
Ling is one of the four Oriental Fighters, heroes inspired by the ancient Four Symbols.

He carries the legacy of the Vermilion Bird, the guardian of the South and the symbol of fire. His teal forehead mark, feathered blue-and-cyan attire, and tempestuous swordplay all echo that celestial inheritance. He may move like cold wind, but something fiery burns beneath his calm.

The other Oriental Fighters embody their own guardians. Zilong represents the Azure Dragon of the East, spear in hand, loyal and radiant with disciplined courage. Baxia represents the Black Tortoise of the North, broad, armoured, steadfast, and immovable, carrying the weight of defence like a fortress given human form. Wanwan represents the White Tiger of the West, swift, sharp-eyed, playful, and dangerous with crossbow and needle-like precision.

Together, they form a complete circle of celestial balance.

Ling's place among them is complicated. He fights beside Zilong when the need arises, but never forgets their unfinished business. The tension between them is quiet, constant, and unmistakable.

"I am the Vermilion Bird," Ling says. "I will protect the South with my blade."

He means it.

But protection does not erase resentment. Duty does not heal humiliation. Ling can stand beside Zilong in battle and still dream of the duel that will prove whether the Great Dragon chose correctly.

That contradiction is part of him now.

chapters.title: The Mysterious Member
chapters.shortDesc: Ling remains the most unreadable Oriental Fighter, respected but not understood, especially by Wanwan.
chapters.fullDesc:
Ling is the most mysterious member of the Oriental Fighters.

Like a ghost, this grim assassin and master of Qinggong lingers outside the Cadia Riverlands, appearing only when needed. His sword is like a tempest when he waves it. His whereabouts are impossible to predict.

He does not speak of his past. He does not explain his actions. He appears, fights, and vanishes. The others respect him, but they do not always understand him.

Wanwan once tried. She came to him on a moonlit roof after a battle, her crossbow folded at her side, her bright eyes studying him with more patience than he expected.

"Why do you not trust us?" she asked.

Ling did not look at her. "Because I have trusted before."

"And you were betrayed?"

"Yes."

"Zilong did not betray you," Wanwan said softly. "The Great Dragon made a choice. That is not the same."

Ling's hand tightened around the Tempest Blade.

"It is the same to me."

Wanwan did not press further. She understood that some wounds were too deep to heal by naming them correctly.

Baxia respected Ling's silence. Zilong carried it like a burden. Wanwan watched it like a locked door she might one day open.
