Thamuz watched from the shadows, his eyes gleaming with approval. Alice watched from the throne, her lips curved in a smile of satisfaction.

He was ready.

chapters.title: The Abilities of the Prince of the Abyss
chapters.shortDesc: An overview of Dyrroth's combat skills: Wrath of the Abyss passive, Burst Strike, Spectre Step, and the devastating Abysm Strike ultimate.
chapters.fullDesc:
Dyrroth's combat style is defined by his demonic heritage—the Wrath of the Abyss that flows through his veins, the hunger for destruction that drives him forward. He is a fighter, a brawler, a berserker who thrives on chaos and carnage.

Wrath of the Abyss (Passive) — The foundation of Dyrroth's power. When Dyrroth's Rage reaches 50%, he enhances his first two active skills, Burst Strike and Spectre Step. After every two basic attacks, Dyrroth releases a Circle Strike, dealing physical damage to enemies in the circle and recovering a percentage of his Max HP—7% to 10% of his Max HP, scaling with his level, halved against minions.

The passive is what makes Dyrroth so dangerous in prolonged engagements. The Circle Strike heals him, allowing him to sustain through fights that would kill lesser heroes. He has two Rage bars, letting him cast enhanced Burst Strike and Spectre Step consecutively. Each time he damages an enemy, the cooldown of Burst Strike and Spectre Step is reduced by 1s, ensuring that his abilities are always available, that he can keep attacking, keep healing, keep killing.

Burst Strike (Skill 1) — Dyrroth's primary ranged tool, a technique that allows him to deal damage to enemies at a distance. He releases a burst strike in a designated direction, dealing physical damage to enemies and slowing them by 25% for 1.5 seconds. The damage decays against the same target and decreases to only 75% on minions.

When enhanced by the Wrath of the Abyss, Burst Strike has a longer range, deals 140% of the original damage, and its slowing effect is doubled—a 50% slow that can stop an enemy in their tracks and set them up for Dyrroth's follow-up attacks.

Spectre Step (Skill 2) — Dyrroth's mobility and crowd control tool, the technique that allows him to close the gap between himself and his enemies. He dashes in the designated direction, stopping when he has traveled the max distance or hits an enemy hero or creep, dealing physical damage to the target and slightly knocking them back. He can then use the skill again within a brief window, locking onto a target and releasing a Fatal Strike, dealing additional physical damage and reducing the target's Physical Defense by 40% for 4 seconds.

When enhanced by the Wrath of the Abyss, the Fatal Strike reaches further, deals 150% of the original damage, slows the target by an extra 90%, and reduces the target's Physical Defense by 60% for 4 seconds—a devastating debuff that can turn even the tankiest hero into a squishy target.

Abysm Strike (Ultimate) — Dyrroth's most devastating technique, the skill that has earned him the title of "Prince of the Abyss." He quickly charges and releases a Fatal Strike, dealing physical damage equal to 650 (+250% Extra Physical Attack) plus 20% of enemies' lost HP to enemies along the way and slowing them by 55% for 0.8 seconds.

The ultimate is Dyrroth's finishing move, the technique he uses to destroy enemies who have been softened up by his Burst Strike and Spectre Step. The damage scales with the target's missing health, making it an excellent execution tool against wounded enemies.

chapters.title: The Masterpiece of Alice
chapters.shortDesc: Alice considered Dyrroth her greatest work—a weapon of deception, strategy, and savagery, now ready to lead the Abyss's Dawn Plan.
chapters.fullDesc:
To Alice, Dyrroth was not merely a weapon. He was her masterpiece, the culmination of decades of planning and patience, the finest work of her dark artistry. She had stolen him from his cradle, raised him in her image, and moulded him into the perfect instrument of destruction.

He mastered Alice's trick, deception, and military strategy. He could lie with the ease of breathing, could read the weaknesses in an enemy's character with a single glance, could turn the most loyal ally into a treacherous enemy with a whispered word. He had learned these skills not from books or lectures, but from living with Alice, from watching her manipulate the demons of the Abyss, from copying her techniques until they became second nature.

Thamuz had taught him to fight. Alice had taught him to think. Together, they had forged him into something the Land of Dawn had never seen—a prince of two worlds, a hybrid of light and darkness, a weapon that could not be matched.

Dyrroth's maturity symbolized the greatness of the Demons. They finally got the new Son of the Abyss. Alice embraced the beloved fighter and recalled the Royal Plan that she had carried out. He was a masterpiece to her.

He would represent the Lord of the Abyss, fighting against the Moniyan Empire, implementing the "Dawn Plan", and destroying the "Shining Spark" of the Empire.

Dyrroth accepted his role without question. He had no reason to question it. The Moniyan Empire was a distant memory, a story that Alice had told him about a family that had abandoned him. The Abyss was his home. Alice was his mother. Thamuz was his teacher. The demons were his brothers.

Why would he ever want to return to a world that had let him be stolen?

chapters.title: The Invasion Begins
chapters.shortDesc: Dyrroth stepped into the Land of Dawn, uneasy in the light, his rage growing as he resolved to kill all who occupied the world.
chapters.fullDesc:
The day came when Dyrroth was deemed ready to serve his purpose. He left the Abyss, carrying the mission to attack the Moniyan Empire.

The smell of the new world made him suddenly feel uneasy. He had been raised in the darkness of the Abyss, where the air was thick with sulphur and the light was a dim, crimson glow. The Land of Dawn was different—the air was cleaner, the light was brighter, the sounds were softer. It was unsettling, alien, wrong.

He stopped at the edge of the Southern Hills, looking out over the land that had once been his home. He thought about whether he could control this world or not.

Then his rage began to grow.

He did not remember the Moniyan Empire. He did not remember the palace, the nursery, the sister who had sung to him. The demons had burned those memories away, replacing them with darkness and hunger and the endless drive to destroy. All he knew was that this world had rejected him, that his family had abandoned him, that the light was a lie.

He believed that his birth had some important meanings to this world. He should kill all creatures who occupied this world. No matter who they were and strong they were, Dyrroth wanted to be the most powerful person in this world.

He stepped out.

There were no survivors to tell his stories. No survivors to warn humanity of its handsome demise.

chapters.title: The Duel with the Lightborn
chapters.shortDesc: Dyrroth faced his sister Silvanna and the Lightborn, driving them back and vowing to destroy everything she loved.
chapters.fullDesc:
The Moniyan Empire did not fall easily. The Lightborn—the elite squad of heroes assembled by Silvanna—stood in Dyrroth's way, their powers combined in a desperate attempt to stop the Prince of the Abyss.

Silvanna faced her brother for the first time in decades. She had imagined this moment a thousand times—had dreamed of it, rehearsed it, prepared for it. She had imagined that she would see something in his eyes, a flicker of recognition, a spark of the boy she had once loved.

She saw nothing. Only hunger. Only rage. Only darkness.

"Brother," she said, her voice trembling, her lance raised. "I will bring you home."

Dyrroth laughed. It was a cold, bitter sound, devoid of warmth, devoid of humanity.

"I have no home," he said. "I have no sister. I have no brother. I have only the Abyss, and the Abyss has only me."

The duel was brutal, savage, and desperate. Silvanna had trained her entire life for this moment, had honed her skills to the peak of perfection, had surrounded herself with the strongest heroes in the empire. But Dyrroth was not just a fighter; he was a force of nature, a storm of darkness and fury that could not be stopped.

He unleashed the full power of the Wrath of the Abyss, his Rage bars filled, his abilities enhanced, his fists blazing with crimson flames. He drove back the Lightborn, one by one, until only Silvanna remained.

He stood over her, his fist raised, his eyes blazing.

"I will destroy everything you love," he said. "I will burn your empire to the ground. I will erase every memory of the Moniyan dynasty from the face of the Land of Dawn. This is my purpose. This is my promise."

He did not kill her. He could have—she was wounded, defenceless, at his mercy—but he did not. Something stayed his hand, some flicker of the boy he had once been, some echo of the sister who had sung him lullabies.

He turned and walked away, leaving her bleeding on the ground.

"Next time," he said, without looking back. "Next time, I will not hesitate."

chapters.title: The Philosophy of the Abyss
chapters.shortDesc: Dyrroth believes only in power, loyalty to Alice, and his destiny to destroy all who occupy the world.
chapters.fullDesc:
Dyrroth does not believe in redemption. He has seen too much suffering, too much darkness, too many souls crushed beneath the weight of the Abyss to believe that anyone can be saved. Redemption is a lie that the weak tell themselves to justify their failure to act.

He believes in power. Power is the only currency that matters, the only truth that cannot be denied, the only force that can shape the world. The strong rule, the weak serve, and the foolish dream of a world where justice is more than a weapon wielded by the victor.

"All creatures who occupy this world will die," he says. "No matter who they are or how strong they may be, I will be the one to destroy them. This is my purpose. This is my destiny."

He does not hate the Moniyan Empire. Hatred would imply that he cared, that he had some emotional investment in its destruction. He is simply fulfilling his purpose, carrying out the plan that Alice had designed for him, playing the role that had been chosen for him before he could walk.

He also believes in loyalty. Not the blind loyalty of a soldier to his general, but the deep, abiding loyalty of a son to his mother. Alice had raised him, protected him, taught him everything he knew. She had given him a purpose when the world had given him nothing. He would die for her. He would kill for her. He would burn the world to ashes for her.

That is the philosophy of the Abyss. It is not complicated. It is not elegant. It is enough.

chapters.title: The Bond with Silvanna
chapters.shortDesc: Silvanna never stopped searching for her brother, but Dyrroth, now the Abyss's champion, has severed all bonds with the light.
chapters.fullDesc:
The relationship between Dyrroth and Silvanna is the most tragic bond in the Land of Dawn. They are siblings, bound by blood, separated by darkness. They love each other—or at least, they love the memory of each other—but that love is not enough to bridge the chasm that separates them.

Silvanna never gave up her vigilant search for him, while Alice, her abductor, meticulously shaped him into the Abyss's fiercest and most loyal champion.

Though not born of demon blood, Dyrroth flourished in the depths of the Abyss by embracing its savage nature. In a realm where power is revered above all, he willfully hastened his own corruption to prove his allegiance, reforging his flesh in the darkness and severing all bonds with the light.

Silvanna's voice calls to him sometimes, in the quiet moments between battles. He hears her saying "brother, I will bring you home," and for a moment, a flicker of something—regret? longing? memory?—passes through his crimson eyes.

Then the moment passes, and the darkness returns.

"I am not your brother," he tells her, when their paths cross. "The boy you knew died a long time ago. I am what remains. I am the Prince of the Abyss. And I will never go home."

Silvanna does not give up. She cannot give up. She has spent too many years searching, too many nights praying, too many battles fighting to save him. She believes—against all evidence, against all reason—that somewhere within the darkness, her brother still lives.

She is wrong. Or perhaps she is right. The truth is hidden so deep that even Dyrroth does not know it anymore.

chapters.title: The Legacy of the Prince of the Abyss
chapters.shortDesc: Dyrroth does not fear death, only wonders if anyone will mourn him, before stepping out to continue his endless war.
chapters.fullDesc:
Dyrroth does not think about legacy. He does not think about what will be said about him after he is gone, because he does not expect to be gone. He is the Prince of the Abyss, the Son of Darkness, the masterpiece of Alice's Royal Plan. He will fight until the Moniyan Empire falls, until the Lightborn are scattered, until the Land of Dawn is remade in the image of the Abyss.

But he is not invincible. He can bleed. He can be wounded. He can die.

He thinks about this sometimes, in the quiet moments between battles, when the darkness is still and the hunger is dormant. He wonders if anyone will mourn him when he falls. He wonders if Silvanna will weep. He wonders if Alice will find a new son to replace him.

Probably not. Probably they will move on, the way the world always moves on, the way the Empire moved on after he was stolen.

He does not let these thoughts trouble him. He is not afraid of death. He is not afraid of anything.

He steps out into the light, his fists clenched, his eyes blazing, and he prepares for the next battle.

There are no survivors to tell his stories. No survivors to warn humanity of its handsome demise.

He is Dyrroth, the Prince of the Abyss. And he is still fighting.

chapters.title: The Eternal Silence
chapters.shortDesc: Under the moon, Dyrroth gazes at Lumina City, feeling nothing but rage, and begins his march to destroy the Shining Spark.
chapters.fullDesc:
"Thirty years ago, a prince was born in the Moniyan Empire. On the day of the prince's first birthday he disappeared, and sorrow befell the whole Moniyan Empire. The Empire Nobles appointed the Imperial Knights and the Monastery of Light to find the truth. At the same time, the Son of Darkness, Dyrroth, was born too. The Demons nourished him with Demons Blood. Integrated with Wrath of the Abyss since childhood, Dyrroth was surrounded by a protective shield. No matter who touched him, they would not withstand the wrath."

— From the mastery records of the Monastery of Light

The night is quiet in the Southern Hills. The moon hangs low in the sky, casting silver light across the plains that stretch toward the Moniyan Empire. Dyrroth stands at the edge of the Abyss, his crimson eyes fixed on the horizon, his fists clenched at his sides.

He can see the lights of Lumina City in the distance—the capital that should have been his, the throne that should have been his, the people who should have been his subjects. He feels nothing. No longing, no regret, no nostalgia. Only the cold, steady rhythm of his anger.

He is not the prince that the Empire mourned. He is not the hero that the people hoped for. He is something else—something darker, something stronger, something that cannot be stopped.

The Demons nourished him with Demons Blood. Integrated with the Wrath of the Abyss since childhood, he was surrounded by a protective shield. No matter who touched him, they would not withstand the wrath.

He steps forward.

The world is waiting. The battle is beginning. And Dyrroth, the Prince of the Abyss, is ready.

He will represent the Lord of the Abyss, fighting against the Moniyan Empire, implementing the "Dawn Plan", and destroying the "Shining Spark" of the Empire.

He steps out.

There are no survivors to tell his stories. No survivors to warn humanity of its handsome demise.

Dyrroth, the Prince of the Abyss, begins his march.

chapters.title: A Compendium of Dyrroth's Powers and Techniques
chapters.shortDesc: Detailed breakdown of Wrath of the Abyss (Passive), Burst Strike, Spectre Step, and Abysm Strike (Ultimate).
chapters.fullDesc:
The Nature of His Power

Dyrroth's power is demonic in origin—the product of the Demon Blood that flows through his veins and the Wrath of the Abyss that has been integrated into his being since childhood. He was not born with these powers; they were given to him, forced upon him, woven into his flesh and soul by Alice and the demons of the Abyss.

The Wrath of the Abyss manifests as a Rage bar below his health, a measure of his anger and his hunger. As he fights, his Rage grows, and when it reaches certain thresholds, his abilities become enhanced—longer range, more damage, greater crowd control. He has two Rage bars, allowing him to cast enhanced Burst Strike and Spectre Step consecutively.

The source of his power is also the source of his corruption. The Demon Blood that nourished him as a child continues to flow through his veins, and the Wrath of the Abyss that surrounded him as a protective shield still burns within his soul. He cannot escape it, cannot purge it, cannot be anything other than what he has become.

Wrath of the Abyss (Passive)

This passive ability is the foundation of Dyrroth's power, a technique that rewards his aggression and sustains him in battle. When Dyrroth's Rage reaches 50%, he enhances his first two active skills, Burst Strike and Spectre Step. After every two basic attacks, Dyrroth releases a Circle Strike, dealing physical damage to enemies in the circle and recovering a percentage of his Max HP—7% to 10% of his Max HP, scaling with his level, halved against minions.

The passive also reduces the cooldown of Burst Strike and Spectre Step by 1 second each time Dyrroth damages an enemy, allowing him to use his abilities more frequently in prolonged engagements. Dyrroth recovers 2% to 5% Rage per second, scaling with his level, ensuring that his Rage bars are always filling, always ready for the next enhanced ability.

Burst Strike (Skill 1)

Dyrroth's first ability is his primary ranged tool, a technique that allows him to deal damage to enemies at a distance. He releases a burst strike in a designated direction, dealing 240 (+60% Total Physical Attack) physical damage to enemies and slowing them by 25% for 1.5 seconds. The damage decays against the same target and decreases to only 75% on minions.

When enhanced by the Wrath of the Abyss, Burst Strike has a longer range, deals 140% of the original damage, and its slowing effect is doubled—a 50% slow that can stop an enemy in their tracks and set them up for Dyrroth's follow-up attacks.

Spectre Step (Skill 2)

Dyrroth's second ability is his mobility and crowd control tool, the technique that allows him to close the gap between himself and his enemies. He dashes in the designated direction, stopping when he has traveled the max distance or hits an enemy hero or a Creep, dealing 230 (+60% Extra Physical Attack) physical damage to the target and slightly knocking them back. He can then use the skill again within a brief window, locking onto a target and releasing a Fatal Strike, dealing 345 (+120% Extra Physical Attack) physical damage and reducing the target's Physical Defense by 40% for 4 seconds.

When enhanced by the Wrath of the Abyss, the Fatal Strike reaches further, deals 150% of the original damage, slows the target by an extra 90%, and reduces the target's Physical Defense by 60% for 4 seconds—a devastating debuff that can turn even the tankiest hero into a squishy target.

Abysm Strike (Ultimate)

Dyrroth's ultimate ability is his most devastating technique, the skill that has earned him the title of "Prince of the Abyss." He quickly charges and releases a Fatal Strike, dealing physical damage equal to 650 (+250% Extra Physical Attack) plus 20% of enemies' lost HP to enemies along the way and slowing them by 55% for 0.8 seconds.

The ultimate is Dyrroth's finishing move, the technique he uses to destroy enemies who have been softened up by his Burst Strike and Spectre Step. The damage scales with the target's missing health, making it an excellent execution tool against wounded enemies.

chapters.title: On the Prince of the Abyss
chapters.shortDesc: Dyrroth, the stolen prince reborn in darkness, will continue fighting, surrounded by the Wrath of the Abyss, with no survivors to tell his stories.
chapters.fullDesc:
Dyrroth. Prince of the Abyss. Son of Darkness. The titles accumulate, each one a weight, each one a reminder of the purpose that drives him and the darkness that defines him.

He was born a prince of the Moniyan Empire, a symbol of salvation and justice for his people. He was stolen on his first birthday, kidnapped by Alice, the Queen of the Blood Demons, and dragged into the Abyss. He was nourished with Demon Blood, integrated with the Wrath of the Abyss, and trained by Thamuz to be the perfect weapon.

He is not the prince that the Empire mourned. He is not the hero that the people hoped for. He is something else—something darker, something stronger, something that cannot be stopped.

The Demons nourished him with Demons Blood. Integrated with the Wrath of the Abyss since childhood, he was surrounded by a protective shield. No matter who touched him, they would not withstand the wrath.

He will represent the Lord of the Abyss, fighting against the Moniyan Empire, implementing the "Dawn Plan", and destroying the "Shining Spark" of the Empire.

He steps out.

There are no survivors to tell his stories. No survivors to warn humanity of its handsome demise.

He is Dyrroth, the Prince of the Abyss. And he is still fighting.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Machine
chapters.shortDesc: Saber wakes as a weapon without a name, but the sword remembers Duan Meng, Zhixu, and the life Laboratory 1718 tried to erase.
chapters.fullDesc:
"They erased my name. They erased my memories. They erased everything that made me human. But they could not erase the sword. The sword remembers. The sword always remembers."

Saber does not know whether he said those words aloud or only heard them in a dream. He does not know whether the ghost who answered was real. He knows only that the name Duan Meng still echoes somewhere beneath the metal.

There is a particular silence that falls over a cyborg's mind when the memories stop fighting. It is not peace. Peace is warm, soft, and alive with birdsong. This silence is a factory floor at midnight, machines powered down but not disconnected, circuits humming with energy that has nowhere to go.

Saber has known that silence since the day he woke in Laboratory 1718 with no memory of who he was.

He does not know his real name, birthday, mother's face, father's voice, or the smell of the village where he grew up. Those things were stripped from him like corrupted data, replaced with combat protocols, targeting algorithms, and the cold logic of a weapon.

But the sword remembers.

The sword remembers a bamboo blade in a child's hands. It remembers humiliation, defeat, obsession, and the desperate hunger to become sharper than every living man. It remembers the swordsman who existed before crimson visor, synthetic heart, and cybernetic limbs.

It remembers Duan Meng.

Saber does not know if Duan Meng still lives inside him. He does not know if the memories flickering at the edge of consciousness are authentic or manufactured. He knows only that somewhere in the Land of Dawn waits a name: Zhixu.

He must find him.

This is the story of a man who sold his soul for a sharper edge, a machine that learned to dream, and a wandering sword searching for the past it may never recover.

chapters.title: The Golden Boy of the Tianyin Swordmaster Sect
chapters.shortDesc: Before Saber, there was Duan Meng, a village boy taken by Master Longma to the Tianyin Swordmaster Sect.
chapters.fullDesc:
Before there was Saber, there was Duan Meng.

His name meant "Duan's Dream" in the old tongue of the Cadia Riverlands, fitting for a boy who dreamed of becoming the greatest swordsman the world had ever seen. He was born in a small village at the foot of the Misty Mountains, son of a farmer who had never held a sword and a mother who died giving him life.

His father, grieving and distant, did not know what to do with a son who spent more time carving wooden swords than tending crops.

Duan Meng taught himself to fight. He watched travelling swordsmen pass through the village, memorising stances, strikes, and subtle shifts of weight. He practised behind the barn where his father could not see him wasting time on useless dreams.

He was eight when Master Longma found him.

Longma was old, with white brows, a weathered face, and robes patched from decades of travel. A disciple of the Great Dragon and master of the Tianyin Swordmaster Sect, he wandered the Cadia Riverlands seeking students with the spark of true talent.

He watched Duan Meng for an hour. The boy's form was crude, full of mistakes, but his spirit was a blade waiting to be forged.

Longma offered him a choice: stay in the village and tend fields, or come to the Sect and learn the way of the sword.

Duan Meng did not hesitate.

He left that night with a change of clothes and the wooden sword he had carved with his own hands.

He never saw his father again.

chapters.title: The Disciple Who Outshone His Masters
chapters.shortDesc: Duan Meng becomes the Tianyin Sect’s golden prodigy, but praise turns his discipline into arrogance.
chapters.fullDesc:
The Tianyin Swordmaster Sect was everything Duan Meng had dreamed of and nothing he expected.

The monastery perched on a plateau high in the Misty Mountains, its wooden buildings weathered by wind and snow, its training grounds slick with ice for half the year. Students were few. Master Longma believed in quality over quantity, and every disciple trained from dawn until dusk, six days a week, with the seventh reserved for meditation.

Duan Meng threw himself into the training with ferocity. He rose before dawn, practised until his hands bled, and studied ancient sword texts until his eyes burned. Techniques that should have taken years settled into his body in months.

He surpassed students who had been training for decades before he was born.

He became the Golden Boy: the prodigy, the future of the Sect, the child whose blade seemed destined to carry Tianyin's legacy into history.

But praise is a dangerous whetstone.

Duan Meng began to look down on other students. He mocked their slow progress and sneered at failure. He stopped listening to Longma's lessons, believing he already knew everything the old master could teach.

Longma saw the darkness growing in him. He warned Duan Meng that the sword was not a tool for proving superiority, but a path to self-understanding.

Duan Meng did not listen.

At nineteen, he left the Sect against Longma's orders, descending the mountain with nothing but his sword and pride.

He would not return for three years.

chapters.title: The Wall Called Zhixu
chapters.shortDesc: Duan Meng’s legend collapses when Zhixu defeats him without attacking, exposing the emptiness behind his pride.
chapters.fullDesc:
The world outside the Sect was not what Duan Meng expected.

He imagined rivals waiting to be humbled and victories waiting to be savoured. Instead, he found a world that did not care about his reputation, did not tremble at the Tianyin name, and had never heard of the Golden Boy.

So he made them hear.

He fought across the Cadia Riverlands, challenging every swordsman he could find. He won far more than he lost. Bards sang of him. Nobles invited him to courts. Warriors sought him out to test themselves against the famous Duan Meng.

He began to believe his own legend.

Then he met Zhixu.

Zhixu was a wanderer with no visible school, simple clothes, a simple sword, and an expression closer to boredom than respect. They fought in a clearing outside Thornhaven while a crowd gathered to watch Duan Meng humble another challenger.

The fight lasted less than a minute.

Zhixu did not attack. He stood with sword at his side and waited. Duan Meng unleashed a storm of strikes that should have overwhelmed anyone. Zhixu deflected each one with the ease of brushing away dust.

When Duan Meng exhausted himself, Zhixu spoke.

"You are not ready. Come back when you are."

Then he walked away.

Duan Meng remained in the clearing, humiliated before the crowd, his pride broken more cleanly than bone.

For the first time, his sword felt heavy.

chapters.title: The Three Years of Hell
chapters.shortDesc: Duan Meng trains for three brutal years, returns to Zhixu, and watches his sword snap in half.
chapters.fullDesc:
Duan Meng retreated to the mountains.

He found a cave above the tree line, where air was thin and cold cut like a blade. He built a fire, sharpened his sword, and began to train.

He trained for three years.

He spoke to no one. He ate what he could hunt, drank melted snow, and slept only when his body failed. Days blurred into weeks, weeks into months, months into years. He lost track of time, place, and self.

All that remained was the sword.

When he emerged, he was leaner, harder, colder. His eyes, once bright with ambition, were flat and empty. He had broken himself down and rebuilt himself around one purpose.

He found Zhixu in the same clearing, as if the wanderer had never left.

They fought.

This time, the fight lasted longer. Duan Meng was faster, stronger, and more precise. His strikes came in relentless waves, each designed to wear down Zhixu's perfect defence.

Zhixu did not wear down.

When Duan Meng finally paused to breathe, Zhixu attacked for the first time. The strike was simple: a single thrust moving through the air with terrifying calm. Duan Meng saw it coming. He raised his sword to block.

Zhixu's blade slipped past his guard, struck the hilt, and snapped Duan Meng's sword in two.

The world went silent.

Zhixu sheathed his sword and walked away without another word.

Duan Meng sank to his knees with broken steel in his hands. He had sacrificed everything, and it was not enough.

He would never be enough.

chapters.title: The Bargain with the Devil
chapters.shortDesc: Desperate for perfection, Duan Meng volunteers for Laboratory 1718 and signs away name, memory, and humanity.
chapters.fullDesc:
Laboratory 1718 did not appear on any map.

It was hidden on an island south of the Agelta Drylands, accessible only by boat, magic, or invitation from people who should never be trusted. It was a monument to ambition without ethics, progress without compassion, and the belief that human beings were raw material to be refined into weapons.

Duan Meng came voluntarily.

He had heard rumours in the taverns of Los Pecados: scientists who could enhance the body, replace flesh with steel, and turn ordinary men into gods. Once, he would have dismissed such stories as desperation.

Now he was desperate.

He surrendered himself to the scientists of Laboratory 1718, signing away his name, memories, and humanity. He did not read the contract. He did not care what it said. He wanted only to be better, stronger, worthy.

The process took six months.

They replaced limbs with cybernetic prosthetics, eyes with optical sensors, and heart with a synthetic core. They implanted neural interfaces that connected his brain to the laboratory mainframe, allowing him to process information faster than any human. They erased memories, scraping away everything that made him Duan Meng, leaving combat protocols and killing instinct.

The scientists wore white coats, mirrored goggles, and bloodless smiles. To them, he was not a man. He was a prototype.

When they finished, they gave him a new name.

Saber.

He was faster, stronger, and more precise than any human swordsman.

He was perfect.

He was empty.

chapters.title: The Anatomy of a Cyborg
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed portrait of Saber: crimson visor, white top-knot, indigo armour, synthetic core, and machine-forged sword grace.
chapters.fullDesc:
To look at Saber is to see a man remade in the image of efficiency.

He stands just under six feet tall, balancing the lean grace of a swordsman with the dense power of a machine. He is not bulky; Laboratory 1718 valued speed over mass. Synthetic muscle fibres generate explosive force beneath pale skin and segmented armour.

His face is the face of a ghost. Sharp jawline, high cheekbones, straight slender nose, and skin so pale it seems almost translucent, with a faint blue undertone when his systems run hot.

His eyes are hidden behind a heavy wraparound crimson visor. The visor replaces biological sight with optical sensors, glowing ominous red and pulsing with the rhythm of his synthetic core. Through it, Saber sees heat signatures, energy patterns, weak points, and motion predictions.

His hair is stark snowy white, styled in a gravity-defying top-knot that flares like smoke. A red ribbon trails behind it like a stream of blood.

His attire blends samurai austerity and high-tech armour. He wears a deep indigo combat suit patterned with interlocking cerulean plates, sleeveless to free his arms. One arm seems almost organic beneath reinforcement; the other is openly cybernetic, layered with metal, cables, and precision joints.

At the centre of his chest sits a triangular red core, a glowing reactor that hums steadily. It is his heart, battery, and anchor. Without it, he is only metal and memory waiting for a spark.

He carries no shield. His body is his shield. His sword is his defence. His will is his armour.

Saber looks less like a living man than a question forged in steel:

Can a weapon remember it once had a soul?

chapters.title: Orbiting Swords - A Halo of Death
chapters.shortDesc: Saber’s floating energy blades orbit his body, defending, cutting, and responding faster than physical weapons ever could.
chapters.fullDesc:
Saber's signature technique is Orbiting Swords: a ring of floating blades that circle his body, ready to strike at thought-speed.

The swords are not ordinary steel. They are energy constructs forged from the same power that flows through his triangular core, held in place by magnetic fields generated by cybernetic implants. Each blade curves like a crescent, its edge glowing with crimson light matching his visor.

They move independently, responding to Saber faster than muscle could. They attack from multiple angles, strike several targets at once, and return to orbit between heartbeats.

Saber uses them for defence as well as offence. The ring creates a barrier that deflects projectiles, intercepts enemy attacks, and forces opponents to keep distance. Anyone who gets too close risks being shredded by spinning red arcs.

Maintaining the swords is exhausting. It requires constant concentration and channelled energy. Saber cannot keep them active indefinitely; eventually the strain becomes too great, and he dismisses them to recharge.

But while they circle him, he is nearly untouchable.

Enemies describe the sight differently. Some call it a halo. Some call it a machine storm. Survivors remember only red light, cold air, and the sudden knowledge that every angle of escape had already been calculated.

Saber does not call it beautiful.

He calls it functional.

chapters.title: Charge - The Blur of Steel
chapters.shortDesc: Charge turns Saber into a crimson afterimage, crossing the battlefield faster than the eye can follow.
chapters.fullDesc:
Saber's mobility technique is Charge, a burst of speed that lets him cross the battlefield in the blink of an eye.

The idea is simple. The execution is brutal. Saber engages his thrusters, pushes his body to maximum velocity, and rockets toward a target. One moment he is still. The next, he is behind his enemy, sword already completing its arc.

Charge was developed in answer to a problem: his enemies were fast. Demons, assassins, and enhanced targets relied on agility, evasion, and sudden repositioning.

Saber became faster.

The technique requires precise timing. He must calculate trajectory, anticipate enemy movement, and engage thrusters at exactly the right moment. Too early, and the target dodges. Too late, and he overshoots, exposed.

He has practised Charge thousands of times. He could perform it in his sleep, if he still slept.

When Saber charges, he leaves a trail of red light, an afterimage that lingers before fading. It is beautiful in a strange way: a crimson streak across the grey of battle, proof that even machines can become art if built for violence carefully enough.

The afterimage is also a decoy. Enemies strike where Saber was, not where he is.

By the time they understand the difference, the sword has already passed through them.

chapters.title: Triple Sweep - The Executioner’s Combo
chapters.shortDesc: Saber’s ultimate closes distance, carves three precise strikes, and launches the target into helpless execution.
chapters.fullDesc:
Saber's ultimate technique is Triple Sweep, a devastating three-part combo that ends most fights before they truly begin.

It begins with Charge, closing the distance in a heartbeat. The first strike comes as he arrives: a horizontal slash across the torso, precise enough to open armour and flesh in one motion.

The second strike follows immediately, a vertical cut designed to split defence and disrupt the body beneath. Saber does not waste motion. Every angle is calculated. Every impact has purpose.

The third strike is the finisher: a telekinetic thrust that launches the enemy into the air, suspending them helplessly while Saber delivers the final blow. The last strike is not merely physical. It is a pulse of energy travelling through the target, shattering systems, bone, armour, or whatever substitute the enemy possesses.

Triple Sweep is not used lightly. The energy cost is immense, draining Saber's core and leaving him vulnerable afterward. It also demands absolute focus. Hesitation breaks the sequence. Distraction ruins the execution.

But when it works, it works perfectly.

Saber has killed greater demons with Triple Sweep. He has cut down corrupted champions, Abyssal commanders, and things that should not have been able to die.

He does not enjoy it.

He does not regret it either.

The enemy chose their path. Saber chose his.

chapters.title: The Aura of the Executioner
chapters.shortDesc: Standing before Saber feels like standing before inevitability: red pressure, slowed breath, and a targeting system already deciding your end.
chapters.fullDesc:
To stand before Saber is to feel the weight of inevitability.

His aura is not visible to most, but it is palpable: a pressure in the air that tightens the chest and shortens breath. Those sensitive to magic or energy can see it as a faint red glow around his body, flickering like the edge of a dying flame.

The aura intensifies when Saber prepares to strike. It spreads outward, pressing against enemies like physical force. Weapons feel heavier. Movements feel slower. Thoughts become muddy.

Saber has learned to control it, to direct it toward specific targets, to use it as a tool rather than a side effect. When he focuses on an enemy, that enemy feels a cold certainty that death is coming, not as risk, but as conclusion.

Some break under the pressure. They flee, surrender, or beg for mercy.

Saber does not grant mercy. He is not cruel. He simply does not understand the concept in the way humans do. He was made as a weapon, and weapons were not built to forgive.

Other enemies fight harder, driven desperate by the knowledge that escape is impossible. These are the dangerous ones. The ones who might actually hurt him.

Saber kills them first.

In his visor, fear has colour. Panic has movement. Hesitation has a measurable delay.

And every delay is an opening.

chapters.title: The Destruction of Laboratory 1718
chapters.shortDesc: When Duan Meng’s memories fight back, Saber destroys Laboratory 1718 and walks out as a rogue weapon.
chapters.fullDesc:
The memories began returning six months after Saber's activation.

At first they came as fragments: a face he did not recognise, a song he had never heard, warmth that did not belong to synthetic nerves. He dismissed them as glitches, programming errors, malfunctions technicians would correct.

But the fragments did not stop. They grew stronger and more frequent. They intruded on combat protocols, distracting him at critical moments, causing hesitation where there should have been execution.

The technicians tried to suppress the memories, rewrite neural code, and scrub errors from his system.

Nothing worked.

The memories were not errors. They were his. Remnants of Duan Meng, fighting to be remembered.

Saber did not understand what was happening. He only knew the laboratory had become a prison, the technicians jailers, and freedom required destruction.

He waited until night, when the facility was quiet and guards were distracted. Then he activated combat protocols.

The destruction took six minutes.

He moved through Laboratory 1718 like a storm. Orbiting Swords spun. Charge carried him room to room. Triple Sweep ended anyone who tried to stop him. Alarms blared, then died as he disabled them.

In the control room, the head scientist tried to evacuate. He looked at Saber with the same eyes that had watched him be built, programmed, and stripped of humanity.

Saber killed him without hesitation.

When it was over, he stood among ruins, core pulsing with violence. The memories were quiet now.

He walked into the night.

He did not look back.

chapters.title: The Wandering Sword
chapters.shortDesc: Saber spends years drifting across the Land of Dawn, saving people who fear him and searching without knowing why.
chapters.fullDesc:
Saber spent the next five years wandering the Land of Dawn.

He never stayed long. He put down no roots, claimed no home, and accepted no master. He followed roads, crossed borders, and drifted through landscapes that had no place for him.

He did not know what he was searching for. He did not know if he searched for anything at all. He simply moved.

He fought when he had to: defending villages from demon attacks, protecting travellers from bandits, eliminating threats no one else could handle. He did not ask for payment. He did not ask for thanks. He fought, killed, and moved on.

The people he saved looked at him with fear as well as gratitude. They saw the visor, core, mechanical limbs, and orbiting blades. They knew he was not human. They wondered what kind of monster had saved them.

Saber did not care what they thought.

At least, that is what he told himself.

There were moments when children stared not with fear but wonder. Moments when old women left food outside abandoned shrines after he passed. Moments when a farmer bowed so deeply Saber did not know where to look.

Those moments troubled him more than battle.

He was made to kill.

He was not made to be thanked.

Only one thing cut through the emptiness with certainty: a name buried deep inside a memory.

Zhixu.

chapters.title: The Search for Zhixu
chapters.shortDesc: Saber returns to the ruined Tianyin Sect seeking Zhixu, but Master Longma reveals the name is not a man.
chapters.fullDesc:
The name came in a dream that was not a dream.

Zhixu.

Saber did not know who Zhixu was. He did not know why the name mattered. He only knew he had to find him, and that the search gave his life meaning.

He followed rumours across the Land of Dawn, questioning sages, scholars, bandits, beggars, kings, and peasants. No one knew.

No one except Master Longma.

Saber found the old man in the ruins of the Tianyin Swordmaster Sect. Buildings had collapsed. Training grounds lay empty beneath snow. Longma sat on the porch of the main hall, eyes closed, hands resting on his knees.

He did not seem surprised.

"You have come a long way, Duan Meng."

Saber flinched. The name meant nothing. Somehow, it meant everything.

"Zhixu," he said. "Where is he?"

Longma was silent, then shook his head.

"Zhixu is not a person. Zhixu is a state of being: mastery of the sword without attachment, ambition, or self. You sought him because you could not accept that you were not ready. You surrendered humanity because you could not accept that perfection is an illusion."

Saber did not understand. He did not want to understand.

"Where is Zhixu?"

Longma tapped his chest.

"The man you seek is not out there. He is in here."

Saber turned away.

He could not believe him. If Zhixu was not real, then the search was meaningless. If the search was meaningless, then perhaps Saber was too.

He could not accept that.

chapters.title: The Brotherhood of Alpha and the Shadow of Beta
chapters.shortDesc: Saber learns of Alpha and Beta, later weapons from Laboratory 1718, and recognises kinship in machines who woke up.
chapters.fullDesc:
Saber was not the only weapon to escape the legacy of Laboratory 1718.

Alpha and Beta came later, after Saber's rebellion. They were built from the same technology, refined and improved, designed to be more stable and controllable. Alpha was the body: broad-shouldered, armoured, powerful, carrying the brutal strength of a battlefield engine. Beta was the companion unit: a hovering drone, sharp-eyed and tireless, a second mind focused on defence, scouting, and survival.

Together, they were twins in a sense: two halves of a single fighting consciousness.

Saber did not know them at first. He had never fought beside them, never spoken to them, never seen what Laboratory 1718 had made after him. Yet when he heard rumours of them, he felt recognition deeper than memory.

They were like him.

Weapons who had woken up.

Machines searching for meaning in a world that had created them to be meaningless.

Saber did not seek them out. He did not avoid them either. If their paths crossed, they would cross. If they did not, they would not.

He was not sure he wanted to meet them. Looking at Alpha might be like looking into a future he had escaped or a brother he had abandoned. Looking at Beta might remind him that even machines could be made to care for something beyond orders.

The thought unsettled him.

Saber had spent years proving he needed no one.

The possibility that this was untrue frightened him more than any enemy.

chapters.title: The Sword That Never Stops
chapters.shortDesc: Saber arrives too late to save a village, but not too late to punish the demons who destroyed it.
chapters.fullDesc:
"They call me Saber. I do not know if that is my name or my title. I do not know if there is a difference. I only know that I am a sword, and swords are meant to be wielded. But no one wields me anymore. I wield myself. And I am still learning what that means."

Saber said that to a child who asked why he was crying.

The night is cold over the Cadia Riverlands, stars bright through haze from distant fires. Saber stands on a ridge overlooking a valley where a village burns, destroyed by a demon raid that arrived too fast for defenders to respond.

He is too late. The people are dead.

But the demons are still there, celebrating.

Saber descends into the valley. Orbiting Swords spin to life. His core hums. His visor glows red as targeting systems acquire enemies.

The demons see him. They laugh. They charge.

The first wave dies before reaching him. The second hesitates, then charges anyway, driven by Abyssal obedience. They die too.

The third wave tries to flee.

Saber charges. A crimson afterimage paints the valley. The demons fall.

When it is over, Saber stands among bodies, core pulsing with the residue of violence. Fires still burn. Smoke still rises.

He turns and walks away.

He does not know where he is going.

He only knows he cannot stop.

The sword never stops.

chapters.title: A Compendium of Saber's Powers and Techniques
chapters.shortDesc: A compact breakdown of Saber’s cybernetic core, Orbiting Swords, Charge, Triple Sweep, Crimson Visor, and execution aura.
chapters.fullDesc:
The Nature of His Power:
Saber's abilities come from cybernetic enhancements replacing much of his biological body. His power source is the triangular red core embedded in his chest, a miniature reactor converting ambient energy into usable force.

The core is not infinite. When power runs low, his movements become sluggish, thoughts muddled, and systems unstable. Overusing it accelerates degradation. Saber does not know how long he has left.

Orbiting Swords:
Orbiting Swords creates a ring of plasma blades around his body, held by magnetic fields from cybernetic implants. They strike targets with surgical precision and form a defence against projectiles or close-range assaults.

Charge:
Charge engages Saber's thrusters and sends him across the battlefield in a blink. It drains the core and strains his limbs, but creates a red afterimage that confuses enemies and draws fire.

Triple Sweep:
Triple Sweep is a three-part execution: a rapid approach, two precise slashes, and a final energy thrust that launches and destroys the target. It is powerful, costly, and requires absolute focus.

The Crimson Visor:
Saber's visor replaces biological sight with optical sensors. It reads heat, energy, trajectories, weak points, and tactical data. When filters fail, the world becomes overwhelming light and noise.

The Aura of the Executioner:
Saber's presence carries cold inevitability. Allies see a silent protector. Enemies feel death calculating its route toward them.

chapters.title: On the Sword
chapters.shortDesc: Saber is a title, not a name, but he keeps fighting because somewhere inside him Duan Meng still remembers.
chapters.fullDesc:
Saber.

The name is a title, not a name: a description of function rather than identity. Saber is a sword. He was created to be a sword. He has spent his entire existence trying to prove he is more than that.

He does not know if he has succeeded. He does not know if he ever will.

But he knows he is still fighting. He knows he is still searching. Somewhere in the depths of corrupted memory is a fragment of the man he used to be: Duan Meng, who dreamed of becoming the greatest swordsman the world had ever seen.

Saber does not know if he can become that man again.

He does not know if he wants to.

But he will keep searching. He will keep fighting. He will keep wandering.

The sword remembers.

The sword never stops.

Neither will he.

chapters.title: The Foot That Refused to Stay Down
chapters.shortDesc: Chou introduces himself as a street fighter from the slums of Antoinerei who refused to accept his place, using kung fu to kick his way from nothing to something.
chapters.fullDesc: "They said I had nothing. No money. No family. No future. They said I should be grateful for the scraps they threw me, should bow my head and accept my place. I did not bow. I kicked. I kicked the door down. I kicked the walls aside. I kicked until the world had no choice but to make room for me. That is what kung fu is. Not fancy moves. Not ancient wisdom. The refusal to stay down." — Chou, to a young fighter who asked him the meaning of martial arts. There is a particular kind of silence that falls over the slums of Antoinerei at midnight. It is the silence of exhaustion, of a world that has given everything it has just to survive another day. Chou has known this silence since he was old enough to understand what the slums were. He was born in Antoinerei, a district the maps pretend does not exist. No father. No mother. Just a boy who refused to accept that he didn't matter. He fought, scraped, and clawed his way out one kick at a time. This is his story.

chapters.title: Antoinerei — The City That Forgave Nothing
chapters.shortDesc: Chou's childhood in the slums: stealing to survive, sharing food with the elderly, and learning to read from an old man in a collapsed tenement.
chapters.fullDesc: Antoinerei was not a place where children were supposed to grow up. The buildings were crumbling, the streets dark even at noon, the air thick with smoke and sewage. The people were the empire's forgotten—the desperate, the broken, the unwanted. Chou did not remember his parents. He survived by stealing, not by choice but necessity. He was small, quick, and smart. But he was also kind. He shared his stolen food with the old people of the slums, helped them carry water, chased away bullies. They called him 'Little Tiger.' An old man in a basement taught him to read from a torn book. Chou learned that the world was bigger than Antoinerei, and he resolved to fight his way to it.

chapters.title: The Old Monk Who Changed Everything
chapters.shortDesc: Chou saved an old monk named Master Tien from a mob, and in return the monk taught him the ancient art of kung fu.
chapters.fullDesc: The monk came to Antoinerei on a night of rain. He was old, with skin like cracked leather and eyes that seemed to see through walls. A mob was chasing him—well-dressed outsiders shouting about heresy. Chou tripped the front runners, threw rocks at their torches, and led them on a chase through the alleys until they gave up. He hid the monk in the basement of a collapsed tenement. 'Thank you, child,' the monk said. 'You have a good heart.' His name was Master Tien, a disciple of an ancient order scattered by war. Chou asked to be taught. 'The path is hard,' Master Tien warned. 'It will hurt. It will change you.' Chou answered, 'I do not want to be the same person. The person I am now is nobody.' And so the training began.

chapters.title: The Training That Broke Him and Rebuilt Him
chapters.shortDesc: Brutal training under Master Tien: learning to breathe, to stand, to fall, and finally to kick. Months of discipline transformed the street rat into a martial artist.
chapters.fullDesc: The training was brutal. Master Tien did not teach forms at first. He taught Chou to breathe—to control his breath, slow his heart, calm his mind. He taught Chou to stand—to find his centre, root himself to the ground. He taught Chou to fall—to roll with impact, rise without injury. Chou hated it. He wanted to fight. 'The fight is not the enemy,' Master Tien said. 'The enemy is inside you. Your fear. Your anger. Your pride.' Months passed. The breathing became easier. Then came the kicks: front kicks, side kicks, roundhouse kicks, spinning kicks, jumping kicks. Chou practised until his legs ached, until the kicks became instinct. Master Tien watched with pride. 'You are ready to leave. To find your own path.' Chou bowed, thanked him, and walked out of the slums forever.

chapters.title: The Way of the Dragon — The Philosophy of the Empty Hand
chapters.shortDesc: The philosophy Master Tien taught: being like water, flowing around obstacles, moving without resistance. A lesson Chou would only fully understand after his own failures.
chapters.fullDesc: Master Tien had taught Chou more than techniques. He taught a philosophy: the Way of the Dragon. It was not about fighting—it was about living. Moving through the world without resistance, without attachment, without fear. Being like water—flowing around obstacles, wearing down stone, finding the path of least resistance. Chou did not fully understand when he left the slums. He was still angry, hungry for validation. He wanted to prove he mattered. The philosophy would come later, after he had made mistakes, after he had failed, after he learned that winning fights was not the same as winning at life. For now, he had his kicks, his speed, his determination. It was enough to start.

chapters.title: The Anatomy of a Kung Fu Boy
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed description of Chou's appearance: silver-white undercut, sharp jawline, tan skin, charcoal tactical jumpsuit with yellow accents, and the 'BANG BANG' on his back.
chapters.fullDesc: To look at Chou is to see a man shaped by the streets. He stands just under six feet, lean and dense, built for explosive speed. His face is sharp—angular jaw, high cheekbones, straight nose. His eyes are dark, piercing, the colour of coffee on a winter morning. His hair is his trademark: stark silver-white in a textured undercut, short on the sides, long and swept forward on top. His skin is a sun-kissed tan, marked by the occasional scar. He wears a dark charcoal tactical jumpsuit with vibrant yellow panels on the shoulders and outer arms. A circular 'MLBB' emblem is on his left breast. His hands are covered in MMA-style grappling gloves—right white, left black with yellow lettering. The trousers have a yellow stripe down each leg. On his back rests an oversized futuristic tonfa, metallic silver and blue. And on his back, printed in comic-book font: 'BANG BANG'.

chapters.title: Jeet Kune Do — The Way of the Intercepting Fist
chapters.shortDesc: Chou's fighting philosophy: strike first, strike fast, strike without warning. No styles, no prisons—only adaptation and interception.
chapters.fullDesc: Jeet Kune Do is not a style. It is a philosophy. Master Tien taught Chou that styles were prisons—the true martial artist adapts to the situation rather than forcing the situation to fit a pattern. Chou took this lesson to heart. His fighting style is a hybrid of everything he learned and everything he invented: kicks like Taekwondo, punches like boxing, movement like capoeira. Unpredictable, fluid, impossible to pin down. The name means 'Way of the Intercepting Fist'—the belief that the best defence is a pre-emptive strike. Chou does not wait for his opponents to attack. He attacks first, attacks fast, attacks without warning. It is not honourable. The old masters would disapprove. But Chou grew up in the slums. He learned that the only unfair fight is the one you lose.

chapters.title: Shunpo — The Blink That Blinds
chapters.shortDesc: Chou's signature mobility technique: a burst of speed so fast it appears as teleportation, disorienting enemies and closing distance in an instant.
chapters.fullDesc: Shunpo is Chou's signature technique—a burst of speed so fast that it appears to be teleportation. The concept is simple: Chou pushes his body to its absolute limit, engaging every muscle fibre, every tendon, every ounce of explosive power. He moves faster than the eye can track, crossing impossible distances between heartbeats. When he reappears, he is already striking. His target is not literally blinded, but mentally disoriented—the sudden shift disrupts their perception, leaves them vulnerable. Chou developed Shunpo during his wandering years, realising his speed was his greatest asset. He trained until the movement became instinct. The technique is exhausting; each use drains his stamina significantly. He uses it sparingly, but when he does, he does not hesitate.

chapters.title: The Way of the Dragon — The Kick That Ends Fights
chapters.shortDesc: Chou's ultimate combo: a Shunpo followed by a flurry of kicks, a launching uppercut kick, and a devastating spinning heel kick that sends enemies flying.
chapters.fullDesc: Chou's ultimate technique is The Way of the Dragon—a legendary combo that ends most fights before they truly begin. It begins with a Shunpo, closing the distance instantly. The first strike is a flurry of kicks—rapid, relentless, driving the enemy back. The second strike is a powerful uppercut-style kick that launches the enemy into the air, suspending them helplessly. The third strike is the final blow: a spinning heel kick that sends the enemy flying across the battlefield, crashing into anything in their path. The technique is devastating, capable of breaking bones and shattering shields. But it is also risky—if any part fails, Chou is left exposed. He has practised it thousands of times, but he still respects its power. He uses it only when victory is the only option.

chapters.title: The Aura of the Street Fighter
chapters.shortDesc: Chou's passive aura: a crackling intensity that energises allies and intimidates enemies, a natural byproduct of his fighting spirit.
chapters.fullDesc: To stand before Chou is to feel the energy of the streets. His aura is not visible to most, but it is palpable—a crackling intensity that raises hairs on the back of the neck, a tension that makes the air feel thick with potential violence. Those sensitive to magic can see it: a faint yellow-white shimmer surrounding his body, flickering like the edge of a flame. The aura intensifies when Chou prepares to fight, spreading outward, pressing against enemies like a physical force. Weapons feel heavier. Movements feel slower. Thoughts feel muddier. Chou has learned to control his aura, to direct it at specific targets. Some enemies break under the pressure—they flee, surrender, beg. Chou does not grant mercy. Not because he is cruel, but because the slums taught him that mercy is a luxury he cannot afford.

chapters.title: Eruditio — The City of Scholars
chapters.shortDesc: Chou wandered to Eruditio, joined the Rangers, and found a new family. He also met Captain Bruno, who became his friend and mentor.
chapters.fullDesc: Chou came to Eruditio by accident, following rumours of a tournament that turned out to be a scam. The City of Scholars was everything he had imagined—tall clean buildings, wide paved streets, people who walked with confidence. He felt like an intruder. He found work at a fighting gym, and the retired Ranger owner saw his potential. 'You should join the Rangers. They need fighters like you.' Chou applied, tested, and was accepted. Captain Bruno was not what he expected—loud, confident, almost arrogant. But Bruno genuinely cared. 'Your kicks are good, but your footwork is sloppy,' Bruno said. 'You need to learn to read your opponent.' Chou trained harder. Bruno became his friend, his mentor, his brother. The polished captain and the rough brawler—unlikely, but perfect together.

chapters.title: Lancelot — The Noble Who Mocked Him
chapters.shortDesc: Chou met the noble knight Lancelot, who mocked his fashion sense. They became unlikely friends, and Lancelot helped Chou upgrade his wardrobe.
chapters.fullDesc: Lancelot was everything Chou despised—rich, privileged, beautiful. They met at a gala. 'So you are the famous Kung Fu Boy,' Lancelot said with a smirk. 'I had heard you were rough around the edges. I did not realise they meant literally.' Chou wanted to punch him. But he remembered Bruno's advice: sometimes protecting means swallowing your pride. He walked away. Lancelot followed and apologised. 'I was testing you. Most would have hit me. You walked away. That takes more strength.' They became unlikely friends. Lancelot's greatest contribution was fashion. 'You look like a walking warning sign,' he said of Chou's jumpsuit. He took Chou shopping, taught him about cuts and fabrics. Chou kept the jumpsuit—it was comfortable, and the 'BANG BANG' made him smile. Lancelot sighed, 'Some people cannot be saved.' But he was smiling too.

chapters.title: The Hero of the Streets
chapters.shortDesc: Chou returns to Antoinerei to help, wins a martial arts tournament, and decides his legacy: to keep fighting for the forgotten.
chapters.fullDesc: Chou returns to Antoinerei whenever he can. He funds schools, clinics, shelters. The people remember him as the boy who shared his food. They call him the Hero of the Slums. He does not like the title—he is just a man who got lucky. But he does what he can. The martial arts tournament in the capital drew fighters from across the empire. Chou entered on a whim. He faced masters, champions, warriors. In the final match, he faced a monk from the Monastery of Light. The fight lasted nearly an hour. In the end, Chou won with a single kick. The crowd chanted his name. He felt pride—not arrogant, but quiet and steady. He knew then that his legacy would not be trophies or titles. It would be the fights he fought for those who could not fight for themselves. He is Chou, the Kung Fu Boy. And he is still kicking.

chapters.title: The Foot That Keeps Kicking
chapters.shortDesc: Chou stands on a rooftop in Eruditio, watching over the city. He does not know what the future holds, but he will keep fighting.
chapters.fullDesc: "They call me the Kung Fu Boy. I did not choose the name. I did not want it. But I have carried it for many years now, and I have learned that names are just words. What matters is what you do. And what I do is fight. That is enough." — Chou, to a young boy in Antoinerei who asked him how to become a hero. The night is warm over Eruditio, the stars bright. Chou stands on the roof of the Rangers' headquarters, his eyes fixed on the horizon. The city is quiet, peaceful. He thinks about the slums, the monk, Lancelot, Bruno. He does not know what tomorrow will bring. But he knows what he will do in the meantime. He will fight. He will protect. He will kick. The foot never stops. And as long as Chou draws breath, there will be someone standing between the darkness and the light.

chapters.title: A Compendium of Chou's Powers
chapters.shortDesc: Detailed breakdown of Jeet Kune Do, Shunpo, The Way of the Dragon, and the Street Fighter's aura.
chapters.fullDesc:
The Nature of His Power: rooted in his body—speed, precision, and relentless determination. No magic, no cybernetics. Only flesh, bone, and will.

Jeet Kune Do (Passive): the Way of the Intercepting Fist—strike first, strike fast, strike without warning.

Shunpo: a burst of speed that appears as teleportation, closing distance instantly.

The Way of the Dragon (Ultimate): a legendary combo—flurry of kicks, launching uppercut kick, spinning heel kick that sends enemies flying.

The Aura of the Street Fighter (Passive): a crackling intensity that energises allies and intimidates enemies.

chapters.title: On the Kung Fu Boy
chapters.shortDesc: Chou will be the Kung Fu Boy not because he wants to be, but because someone has to stand up for the forgotten.
chapters.fullDesc: Kung Fu Boy. The title is a burden, but also a gift. It reminds Chou of the monk who taught him to fight, the slums that shaped him, the people who believe in him. He does not know if he will ever be worthy. But he knows he will try. Every day, in every fight, with every kick. He will be brave. He will be strong. He will be relentless. He will be the Kung Fu Boy. Not because he wants to be. Because he has to be. Because someone has to stand up for the forgotten. And Chou, son of the slums, student of the monk, brother of the Rangers, has decided that someone will be him. The night is dark. The fight is long. The kicks keep coming. And Chou never stops.

chapters.title: The Face Behind the Mask
chapters.shortDesc: Suyou introduces himself as the last exorcist of Zhu'an, the final keeper of the mask of the Immortal Nuo. He carries the burden of his people's faith and the weight of a deity's power.
chapters.fullDesc: "I am the last. The final exorcist of the Nuo. The final keeper of the mask. The final vessel of a power that has been passed down through generations since before the written word. They look at me and see a god. They look at my mask and see divinity. They do not see the man behind the mask—the man who bleeds, who doubts, who fears that he is not worthy of the faith they have placed in him. But that is the burden of the exorcist. That is the weight of the mask. To be the bridge between the mortal and the divine, the vessel through which the power of the Immortal Nuo flows into the world. I did not choose this burden. I was born into it. And I will carry it until the day I die—and perhaps beyond." — Suyou, speaking to the mask before a ritual. Zhu'an was once a bustling city of exorcists, its masks and rituals the pride of the land. But the echoes of malice shattered its peace. One by one the exorcists fell. Suyou is the last. He walks the mortal plane, purging evil and safeguarding hope, a wandering swordsman with a god's mask on his face.

chapters.title: The Cradle of Exorcism
chapters.shortDesc: Zhu'an: a city where the living and dead coexisted, and exorcists were chosen from birth. Suyou was born into an ancient lineage and trained from childhood to wear the mask.
chapters.fullDesc: Zhu'an was not built on conquest or commerce. It was built on something older—a place where the boundaries between worlds were thin, and exorcists walked between them. The Temple of Nuo stood at the city's heart, its walls carved with images of the Immortal Nuo's battles. The exorcists were chosen from birth, their bloodlines traced to the founders. Suyou was born into one of the oldest families. His parents were among the finest exorcists of their generation. They trained him from the moment he could walk. "The mask is not a decoration," his father said. "It is a burden. It will take everything from you. Your youth. Your freedom. Your life." Suyou did not understand then. He would learn.

chapters.title: The Temple of Nuo and the Ritual of the Mask
chapters.shortDesc: At twelve, Suyou underwent the sacred ritual. The mask fused to his face, and he saw a vision of the Immortal Nuo and the darkness that would one day consume his home.
chapters.fullDesc: The Temple of Nuo was a labyrinth of halls, altars, and hidden chambers. At its centre was the Chamber of the Mask, where the sacred relics were stored. When Suyou was twelve, the elders deemed him ready. He knelt on cold stone as incense filled the air and chanting echoed. The mask was placed on his face—dark polished wood, carved with shifting patterns. It pressed against his skin, sank into his bones. A vision came: the Immortal Nuo as a vast, transcendent force. Battles fought, victories, defeats. The faces of exorcists who came before him. And the darkness—the same darkness that would one day consume Zhu'an. He opened his eyes. The mask had sealed itself to his face. "You are ready," the chief elder said. "You are the vessel of the Immortal Nuo."

chapters.title: The Night of Falling Stars
chapters.shortDesc: When Suyou was seventeen, the darkness from the Shadow Swamp overwhelmed Zhu'an. His parents fell defending the temple. Suyou took up the mask and became the last exorcist.
chapters.fullDesc: The darkness came from the south, from the Shadow Swamp—a wave of malevolent energy that swept through Zhu'an like a flood. People screamed and died. The exorcists fought. Suyou's parents stood at the gate of the Temple of Nuo, masks glowing, blades flashing. They poured everything into the barrier. But the darkness was endless. Suyou heard his mother scream, his father's voice raised in a final incantation—then silence. He ran to them, but they lay broken, masks cracked. He picked up the mask of the Immortal Nuo—his father's mask—and placed it on his face. Power surged through him, hot and cold. He raised his blade and charged. The battle lasted three days. He drove the darkness back. The city was ruins. The exorcists were dead. Suyou walked away alone.

chapters.title: The Anatomy of the Exorcist
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed description of Suyou: lean build, pale skin, long dark hair streaked with silver, traditional Zhu'an exorcist robes in dark blue and purple, the mask of the Immortal Nuo fused to his face, and the trident-like Blade of Nuo.
chapters.fullDesc: To look at Suyou is to see a man shaped by loss and duty. He stands about 175 centimetres, lean and wiry—built for explosive movement and precise strikes. His face is hidden behind the mask of the Immortal Nuo: dark polished wood with intricate shifting patterns, narrow eye slits, a grim mouth. Beneath, his features are sharp and angular, his skin pale and almost luminous. A faint blue glow emanates from the mask in the presence of evil. His hair is long and dark, falling past his shoulders, streaked with silver from channelling the deity's power. He wears traditional Zhu'an exorcist robes—dark blue and purple, embroidered with silver stars and moons, loose but reinforced with protective enchantments. A heavy belt holds a ritual short sword and a bundle of exorcism scrolls. His boots are soft and silent. In his hands, the Blade of Nuo: a three-pronged trident of unbreakable wood and unknown metal, glowing with blue light. His aura is calm, focused, sad—the presence of a god barely contained.

chapters.title: The Sacred Relics and the Blade of Nuo
chapters.shortDesc: The mask is the source of Suyou's power; the trident is the expression of it. Both have been passed down through generations, each wearer adding to their strength.
chapters.fullDesc: The mask of the Immortal Nuo is not the only sacred relic Suyou carries. He also wields the Blade of Nuo—a ritual trident with three prongs representing past, present, and future. The shaft is made of dark, unbreakable wood; the prongs are forged from a metal that does not exist in the Land of Dawn, glowing with faint blue light and humming with the deity's power. When Suyou strikes an evil spirit, the prongs disrupt its connection to the world, forcing it to confront its own dissolution. The trident was given to him by his father, passed down through generations. When Suyou holds it, he feels the presence of his ancestors—their hopes, fears, sacrifices. He is not alone. The mask is the source; the blade is the expression. Together, they make him the Mask of the Immortal.

chapters.title: The Abilities of the Mask of the Immortal
chapters.shortDesc: Suyou can shift between Mortal and Immortal forms. His techniques include Blade Surge (mobility/stun), Soul Sever (damage/cleave), and Evil Queller (slow/snipe).
chapters.fullDesc: Suyou's combat style is defined by his ability to shift between two forms. Tap-casting any skill puts him in Mortal form, granting movement speed and faster attacks for chasing and dodging. Hold-casting puts him in Immortal form, increasing basic attack damage to 125% and granting damage reduction that scales with his physical attack (up to 40%). Blade Surge (Skill 1): tap-cast throws the weapon and blinks to it for a slashing attack; hold-cast charges forward, stunning enemies in a rectangle. Soul Sever (Skill 2): tap-cast performs a sweeping attack dealing bonus damage based on the target's lost HP; hold-cast performs three cleaves, recovering HP on the final strike. Evil Queller (Skill 3): tap-cast glides backward and swings, slowing enemies; hold-cast charges a long-range arrow that deals massive damage to the first enemy hit. Suyou is a master of adaptation, switching forms to meet any situation.

chapters.title: The Road to Redemption
chapters.shortDesc: After Zhu'an's fall, Suyou wandered the Land of Dawn, performing exorcisms and protecting villages. He accepted gratitude but never sought it, carrying his burden alone.
chapters.fullDesc: After the fall of Zhu'an, Suyou wandered the Land of Dawn, seeking to make amends for his failure. He could not bring back his city or his parents, but he could protect others. He travelled from village to village, exorcising haunted houses, purifying cursed fields, banishing evil spirits. The people called him the Mask of the Immortal. They did not know his name or his face, but they knew his power. He accepted their gratitude but did not seek it. He was not a hero; he was an exorcist doing his duty. The road was long and lonely. The mask isolated him—people saw a god, not a man. On lonely nights, he asked the mask, "Am I worthy?" The mask did not answer. But he had to be enough. He was the last.

chapters.title: The Faith of the People
chapters.shortDesc: In a village on the edge of the Agelta Drylands, Suyou learned that the power of Nuo comes from the people's faith. Their belief makes the mask more than just a mask.
chapters.fullDesc: The power of the Immortal Nuo comes from the faith of the people. Without their belief, the mask is just a mask. Suyou learned this in a small village on the edge of the Agelta Drylands, where a demon had terrorised the locals for months. The people were sceptical—they had seen charlatans before. "Why should we believe you?" the village elder asked. Suyou touched his mask. "Because I am the last exorcist of Zhu'an. Because I have faced darkness you cannot imagine. Because I carry the power of the Immortal Nuo. And because I have not failed yet." He performed the ritual, channelled the deity's power, drove the demon out. The people watched, their fear turning to awe. When he left, the elder asked how to repay him. "Have faith," Suyou said. "Believe that the darkness can be defeated. That is all I need."

chapters.title: The Mask and the Man
chapters.shortDesc: Suyou has worn the mask so long he forgets his own face. He wonders if the mask has consumed him—but the faith of the people reminds him he is still human.
chapters.fullDesc: Suyou has worn the mask for so long that he sometimes forgets what his face looks like. He has not seen his own reflection in years. He does not know if he could remove the mask even if he wanted to—the ritual fused it to his skin. He wonders if there is anything left of the man he used to be. Has the mask consumed him? Is he now just a vessel, a puppet of the deity? But then he meets people like the villagers of the Agelta Drylands—people who are afraid, desperate, needing someone to believe in. And he knows he is still himself. He is still Suyou. The mask is part of him, but not all of him. The people's faith—their hope—keeps him human. He has not lost himself. Not yet.

chapters.title: The Philosophy of the Exorcist
chapters.shortDesc: Suyou's guiding beliefs: the power of Nuo comes from the people's faith, duty to protect the innocent, and humility in the face of powers greater than himself.
chapters.fullDesc: Suyou does not consider himself a philosopher. He is an exorcist, a wanderer, a survivor. But over the years he has developed a philosophy that guides him. "The power of Nuo comes from the faith of the people." Without their belief, he is nothing. He exists to serve them, not the other way around. He believes in duty—not blind obedience, but the deep abiding duty of a protector to those he has sworn to protect. He is the last exorcist of Zhu'an, and he will carry that burden until he dies. He believes in humility. The mask is a symbol of his power but also a reminder of his limitations. He is not a god; he is a man. He can bleed, fail, die. "The strength to change the world might not be something you're born with—it might be something you earn, one choice at a time, one act of kindness at a time, one step at a time."

chapters.title: The Bond with the People of Zhu'an
chapters.shortDesc: The survivors of Zhu'an are scattered as refugees. Suyou searches for them, offering comfort. He hopes one day to rebuild, but for now he protects them from afar.
chapters.fullDesc: The people of Zhu'an are scattered now—refugees in a world that does not want them. Some have found new homes; others live on the margins, forgotten and alone. Suyou searches for them whenever he can, offering what comfort he can provide. He does not tell them who he is. The mask would give him away, and he does not want their gratitude. He simply wants to know they are safe. "I am the last of my kind," he says. "But I am not the last of my people. They live on, in other cities, in other lands, in the memories we carry." He hopes one day to rebuild Zhu'an, to restore the exorcists, to make the mask unnecessary. But that day is not today. Today there are demons to fight, rituals to perform, people to protect.

chapters.title: The Legacy of the Mask of the Immortal
chapters.shortDesc: Suyou does not know what the future holds, but he will keep fighting. He is the last exorcist, the wandering mask, the vessel of a god and the hope of a people.
