She attacked, and the battle continued. At the end, when Kagura fled, Waguri would whisper, 'One day, sister. One day, you will understand.'

chapters.title: The Fox Mask's Wisdom
chapters.shortDesc: After the hundredth battle, Waguri weeps in the Plum Blossom Garden. The mask tells her to wait, that she cannot force her sister to see. She accepts her role as the waiting Shadow Keeper.
chapters.fullDesc: After the hundredth battle, Waguri sat in the Plum Blossom Garden, mask in her hands, and wept. She had tried everything—mercy, strength, patience, love. Nothing had reached her sister. The mask spoke: 'You cannot force her to see. You can only wait. The light will dim, in time. The shadows will grow. When she is ready, she will come to you.' 'How long?' Waguri asked. 'Eternity, if necessary. You are the Shadow Keeper. Waiting is your purpose.' Waguri looked up at the inverted trees, the glowing blossoms, the darkness that was her home. 'She is not my enemy. She is my sister. I will wait for her. Forever, if I must.' She put the mask on, and the first Shadow Keeper's spirit wrapped around her. 'Good girl. Now rest. Tonight, you are allowed to grieve.'

chapters.title: The Meeting in the Shadows
chapters.shortDesc: Waguri meets Hayabusa, a shadow ninja, while hunting a rogue oni. They understand each other's loneliness and become secret companions, bound by a love they never speak aloud.
chapters.fullDesc: Waguri met Hayabusa while hunting a rogue oni. He was a shadow ninja, sent by the Shadow Accord. They fought the oni side by side, blades flashing, shadows dancing. When it fell, they stood back to back in the darkness. 'You're not what I expected,' he said. 'Neither are you.' He understood her in a way that no one else did—her loneliness, her isolation, the weight of being a creature of shadow. They met in secret, in the spaces between worlds. They talked, sparred, shared silence. Waguri loved him. She had never said it aloud, and she knew he loved her in return, though he had never said it either. They were two creatures of darkness, and their love was a secret they kept even from themselves. But it was there, always there, a warmth in the cold.

chapters.title: The Anatomy of a Shadow Mistress
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed description of Waguri's appearance: slender waist, full hips, massive bust, pale flawless skin, white silk hair, nine shadow tails, fox mask, and revealing black kimono.
chapters.fullDesc: To look at Waguri is to see a woman perfected by darkness. Her waist is impossibly slender, flaring into full, rounded hips and powerful thighs. Her chest is massive, a full, voluptuous form that strains against her delicate kimono. She makes no effort to hide it; her attire is designed to reveal as much as it conceals. Her skin is flawless, pale as moonlight on snow. Her face is heart‑shaped, her features delicate, her smile enigmatic. Her eyes are large, almond‑shaped, a deep liquid purple that ignites to dark red when she unleashes her power. Her hair is a cascade of pure white silk falling past her waist. From her spine, nine shadow tails unfurl, each a plume of darkness that moves with a life of its own. She wears a black kimono, open at the chest, held by a blood‑red obi, slit high on both sides to bare her legs. A fox mask sits pushed up on her head. A plum blossom hairpin adorns her hair, and silver chains chime at her waist.

chapters.title: The Kagegasa — Parasol of a Thousand Shadows
chapters.shortDesc: The Kagegasa is Waguri's weapon and throne. It contains a thousand sealed monsters. Its canopy is tattered, leaking shadow, and each painted pattern holds a bound creature.
chapters.fullDesc: The Kagegasa is not a weapon; it is a throne, a prison, a gateway. It contains a thousand monsters, each sealed within the intricate patterns painted on its canopy. The parasol is larger than Waguri, its canopy deep bruised purple, its ribs of black lacquered wood, its handle carved from the bone of the first demon she summoned. Through tears in the canopy, shadow seeps like smoke. Each pattern—snarling oni, twisting serpents, plum blossoms in darkness—is a seal containing a monster. When Waguri opens the Kagegasa, the seals break and the monsters pour forth: oni of black stone, tengu of shadow wings, kappa of iron claws, and a hundred more. They are bound to her will by a pact of mutual benefit. She can summon them at will, command them with a thought. They fight for her, die for her, and when they fall, she summons them again.

chapters.title: The Demons of the Kagegasa
chapters.shortDesc: Waguri's monster legions: Oni Lords (bodyguards), Tengu Generals (scouts), Kappa Legion (engineers), Shadow Wolves (hunters), Nightmare Steeds (mounts), and The Watcher (secret weapon).
chapters.fullDesc: The monsters sealed within the Kagegasa are beings of intelligence and memory. The Oni Lords—Kurogane, Sekizan, Akuma—are ancient, massive creatures of black stone, her bodyguards and shock troops. The Tengu Generals—seven, named for virtues: Kenjin, Yuuki, Jin, Rei, Makoto, Meiyo, Chuugi—are her scouts, assassins, spies. The Kappa Legion are her engineers and defenders, small but numerous, bound by a hive mind. The Shadow Wolves are her hunters, creatures of pure shadow with violet flame eyes, swift and silent. The Nightmare Steeds are her mounts, living darkness that can fly, run across water, and pass through walls. And The Watcher is her secret weapon, a being of pure abyss, unsummoned except in direst need. It can unmake reality, erase targets from existence, destroy cities. Waguri keeps it sealed in the deepest layer, a last resort for the end of the world.

chapters.title: Koko — The White Bat
chapters.shortDesc: Koko is Waguri's spirit companion, a small white bat that sleeps against her heart. Koko grows into a shield and beacon in battle, and is the only being Waguri trusts completely.
chapters.fullDesc: Koko is not a monster. She is a spirit, a fragment of the first shadow that Waguri summoned, bound as a protector and friend. No larger than a palm, with translucent wings and ruby eyes, Koko sleeps in the folds of Waguri's kimono during the day, nestled against her heart. Her tiny body is warm, her heartbeat a gentle thrum. At night, she flutters around Waguri's head, her soft chittering a comfort. When danger threatens, Koko grows. Her wings expand, her eyes blaze, and she becomes a shield that deflects arrows, a weapon that blinds enemies, a beacon that calls forth monsters. She is the only being Waguri trusts completely, the only soul that has never betrayed her. Waguri whispers her secrets to Koko in the dark hours before dawn—about her sister, about Hayabusa, about her fears. Koko listens, chirps softly, and Waguri feels less alone.

chapters.title: The Architecture of Shadow
chapters.shortDesc: The Inverted Shrine is a living thing with seven layers, built on the wound where the first demon fell. Its altars are carved into the ceiling, and its prayers are written in reverse.
chapters.fullDesc: The Inverted Shrine is not a building; it is a living thing, a creature of stone and shadow that breathes and pulses. Its spires point downward, reaching toward the earth's heart. Its walls are lined with glowing purple crystals. Altars are carved into the ceiling; offerings float upward on currents of shadow. Prayers are written in reverse for the spirits of the deep. The shrine was built on the spot where the first demon fell to an elven blade, a wound that never healed. The darkness that seeps from it is thick and fertile, and the Plum Clan cultivates it to bind monsters. The shrine has seven layers: Hall of Offerings, Chamber of Seals, Plum Blossom Garden, Library of Shadows, Armory of the Damned, Sanctum of the Mask, and the Abyssal Gate—a portal to the void between worlds. Waguri guards it, as her ancestors did.

chapters.title: The Plum Clan
chapters.shortDesc: The Plum Clan has served the shrine for a thousand years, dwindling under persecution. Waguri is now its head, carrying the burden of protecting the darkness from the light priests.
chapters.fullDesc: The Plum Clan has served the Inverted Shrine for a thousand years. They believe darkness is not the absence of light but its mirror, its necessary opposite. They believe monsters are not evil, merely hungry and lost. The clan is small, its numbers dwindling. Light priests have hunted them for generations, driving them deeper into shadows. Waguri is the head of the clan now; her father died three years ago, killed by a sun priest's blade. She avenged him—summoned a tengu lord to tear the priest apart—but the loss still aches. The elders respect her but also fear her. She is more powerful than any Shadow Keeper before her. She does not know what she will do with that power. She only knows she will protect the shrine, protect her monsters, protect the darkness that is her home.

chapters.title: The Rites of Binding
chapters.shortDesc: The sacred binding rites are performed in the Chamber of Seals. The key is not strength but understanding—offering a home and purpose to the monster, never force.
chapters.fullDesc: The rites of binding are the most sacred rituals of the Plum Clan. Performed in the Chamber of Seals beneath the inverted moon, they involve summoning and binding a monster to the summoner's will. Waguri has performed the rites a thousand times. The key is not strength—it is understanding. A monster will not serve a master who fears it, despises it, sees it only as a tool. It will serve only a summoner who sees it as a partner, a friend, a part of the family. Waguri reaches out with her shadow tails, touching the creature's mind, feeling its pain, its hunger, its loneliness. She offers it a home in the Kagegasa, a place where it can rest and be safe. Most monsters accept. The ones that do not are returned to the abyss, unharmed. She does not destroy them. They are not evil—they are just lost.

chapters.title: The Inverted Moon
chapters.shortDesc: Once a year, Waguri leads the Rite of the Inverted Moon to strengthen the seals on the Abyssal Gate. After the ritual, she sits in the garden, thinking of Kagura, hoping for reunion.
chapters.fullDesc: Once a year, on the night of the lunar eclipse, the Plum Clan gathers in the deepest chamber for the Rite of the Inverted Moon. It is a ritual of renewal, to strengthen the seals on the Abyssal Gate and honor the first Shadow Keeper. Waguri leads the ritual, fox mask on her face, shadow tails spread wide. She speaks the ancient words, and the darkness answers. Crystals glow brighter, walls pulse with energy, the gate hums. The ritual takes three hours, and by the end, Waguri is exhausted. But she feels the darkness embrace her, comfort her, renew her. Afterward, she sits alone in the Plum Blossom Garden, Koko in her lap, thinking of Kagura. Her sister is out there in the light, celebrating the summer solstice, not knowing her twin is waiting. Waguri hopes. Because hope is the only light the darkness cannot extinguish.

chapters.title: The Hundredth Battle
chapters.shortDesc: The hundredth battle takes place in a ruined castle. Waguri disarms Kagura again and offers peace, but Kagura flees. Waguri weeps for her sister's blindness.
chapters.fullDesc: The hundredth battle took place in the ruins of an old castle. Kagura attacked at dawn, blades blazing with holy fire. Waguri defended, her shadow tails lashing out. They fought for hours. Waguri tried to reason with her sister. 'We don't have to fight. We can be sisters.' Kagura did not answer; she fought harder. Waguri saw the pain in her sister's eyes—the fear, the loneliness. She understood. In the end, Waguri disarmed Kagura and held her blade at her throat. 'Why do you hate me?' 'I don't hate you. I hate what you represent. The darkness. The evil.' 'The darkness is not evil. It is part of the world, part of the balance. Without shadow, there is no light.' Kagura's eyes widened. For a moment, Waguri saw longing. Then Kagura fled. Waguri watched her go and wept.

chapters.title: The Light Priests' Lies
chapters.shortDesc: Waguri learns that the light priests have manipulated Kagura, lied to her about the darkness. She pities them but vows to protect the shrine from their cruelty.
chapters.fullDesc: Waguri had learned that the light priests were not as pure as they claimed. They had manipulated Kagura, lied to her, used her as a weapon. They told her darkness was evil, the Plum Clan were demons, salvation only through light. They hid the truth: light and shadow are two halves of a whole; the world needs both; balance is the only path to peace. Waguri did not hate the light priests. She pitied them. They were afraid, and fear had made them cruel. But she would not let them destroy her home, her family, her monsters. She would fight them as she had fought them a hundred times. One day, she hoped, Kagura would see the truth. One day, her sister would come to the shrine, not to destroy it, but to understand. Until then, Waguri waited.

chapters.title: The Weight of Loneliness
chapters.shortDesc: Alone in the quiet shrine, Waguri reflects on her sister, Hayabusa, and her father's death. She has learned that loneliness is a teacher, not a curse.
chapters.fullDesc: The shrine was quiet at night. Monsters slept, crystals dimmed, and Waguri sat alone, Koko in her lap, shadow tails curled around her. She thought about Kagura, about the battles they had fought, about the words they had never spoken. She thought about Hayabusa, about secret meetings in spaces between worlds, about love never confessed. She thought about her father, his death, the emptiness he left behind. She was lonely. She had always been lonely, even in the midst of her monsters, even in the warmth of darkness. She was the Shadow Keeper, and the Shadow Keeper walked alone. But she did not despair. Loneliness was not a curse—it was a teacher. It taught her to value connections, cherish moments of companionship, appreciate silence. She closed her eyes, and the darkness held her.

chapters.title: The Memory of Light
chapters.shortDesc: Sometimes Waguri remembers the sun from her childhood. She misses it and wonders if Kagura ever misses the darkness. She hopes a spark of shadow remains in her sister's heart.
chapters.fullDesc: Sometimes, in the quiet moments, Waguri remembered the light. She had not seen the sun since she was a child, but she remembered its warmth, its brightness, its ability to banish shadows. She remembered grass beneath her feet, the smell of flowers, the sound of birds. She missed the light. She missed it fiercely, painfully, hopelessly. She was a creature of shadow, but she had been born under the moon, and the moon was a reflection of the sun. She wondered if Kagura ever missed the darkness. If her sister ever lay awake at night, thinking of shadows, wondering what it would be like to walk in twilight. She hoped so. She hoped the light had not completely consumed her sister, that a spark of shadow still remained. Because without that spark, there was no hope. And without hope, there was nothing.

chapters.title: The Shadow Ninja
chapters.shortDesc: Hayabusa is a creature of darkness like Waguri, trained by the Shadow Accord. They meet in the spaces between worlds, sharing silence and understanding. She loves him.
chapters.fullDesc: Hayabusa was a creature of darkness, like her. Trained by the Shadow Accord, he was not evil—simply practical. He did what needed to be done and did not apologize. He and Waguri met in the spaces between worlds, where the sun never reached. They talked, sparred, shared silence. He understood her in a way no one else did—not her father, not the elders, not even her monsters. She loved him. She had never said it aloud, and she knew he loved her in return, though he had never said it either. They were two creatures of darkness, and their love was a secret they kept even from themselves. But it was there, always there, a warmth in the cold, a light in the shadow. And for Waguri, that was enough.

chapters.title: The Unspoken Words
chapters.shortDesc: Hayabusa tells Waguri that his actions—protecting her, fighting beside her, sharing secrets—are his declaration of love. She accepts his unspoken words and is content.
chapters.fullDesc: They sat on the edge of a floating island, in the space between worlds, feet dangling over the abyss. Hayabusa was silent, as he often was. Waguri watched him, her heart aching. 'You know, you could say it. I wouldn't mind.' 'Say what?' 'You know what.' He was silent for a long moment. Then he turned to her, his eyes reflecting the darkness. 'I am not good at words. I am good at actions. I have protected you. I have fought beside you. I have shared my secrets with you. If that is not love, then I do not know what is.' Waguri smiled. 'It is love. It has always been love.' They sat in silence, watching stars spin slowly above them. Waguri did not need him to say the words. She knew. That was enough.

chapters.title: The Promise
chapters.shortDesc: Before parting, Hayabusa promises to come whenever Waguri needs him, and to stay as long as she needs him. She treasures the promise as a light in the darkness.
chapters.fullDesc: Before they parted, Hayabusa made her a promise. 'If you ever need me, I will come. No matter where I am, no matter what I am doing, I will come.' 'And if I need you to stay?' He looked at her, his eyes soft. 'Then I will stay. For as long as you need me.' Waguri reached out and touched his cheek. 'I will hold you to that.' He nodded, then was gone, swallowed by the shadows. Waguri watched him go, and felt a warmth in her chest that had nothing to do with the light. It was the warmth of love. She waited for him, as she waited for her sister. She did not know if he would ever speak the words, if he would ever stay, if their love would ever be acknowledged. She only knew she loved him, and that love was a light in the darkness.

chapters.title: The Waiting
chapters.shortDesc: Waguri waits for Hayabusa as she waits for Kagura. She dreams of a future where light and shadow coexist, where she can have a family, but she holds only hope.
chapters.fullDesc: She waited for him, as she waited for her sister. She did not know if he would ever speak the words, if he would ever stay, if their love would ever be acknowledged. She only knew that she loved him, and that love was a light in the darkness. She thought about the future—a life together, children who would walk in twilight, a family not defined by light or shadow. She did not know if that future would ever come. She only knew that she hoped. And hope, she had learned, was the only light the darkness could not extinguish. She closed her eyes, the darkness holding her, and she waited.

chapters.title: The Dream of the Twin
chapters.shortDesc: Waguri dreams of Kagura weeping in a field of light. She reaches out, but the light burns her. She wakes, wondering if her sister dreamed the same.
chapters.fullDesc: One night, Waguri dreamed of Kagura. Her sister stood in a field of light, surrounded by sun priests, weeping. 'I don't know what to do. They tell me the shadow is evil, but I see your face in my dreams, and you are not evil. You are just... sad.' Waguri reached out, but the light burned her hand. She pulled back, and the dream faded. She woke with a start, Koko chittering in her ear. The dream had felt real, more real than any before. She wondered if Kagura had dreamed the same thing, if her sister was also waking in the light, confused and afraid. She hoped so. She hoped the dream was a message from darkness to light, a reminder that they were connected, that they were two halves of a whole.

chapters.title: The Sealing of the Abyssal Gate
chapters.shortDesc: The Abyssal Gate weakens from the Sundering. Waguri descends to the seventh layer and seals it with her monsters, exhausting herself but saving the shrine.
chapters.fullDesc: The Abyssal Gate had been weakening for years. The Sundering had torn the fabric of reality, and darkness was seeping through, threatening to consume the shrine. Waguri descended to the seventh layer, her shadow tails spread, her fox mask glowing. She raised the Kagegasa and opened it fully. Monsters poured forth, surrounding the gate, forming a barrier of shadow and flesh. She spoke the ancient words of sealing, and the gate trembled. Darkness screamed. Then slowly, it began to close. Waguri felt her strength draining, her power flowing into the seal. She staggered, almost fell, but Koko grew, wrapping her wings around her, holding her steady. The gate sealed shut. Waguri collapsed, exhausted, her shadow tails limp. She had done it. The shrine was safe. For now.

chapters.title: The Summoning of the Watcher
chapters.shortDesc: The Watcher is Waguri's secret weapon, a creature of pure abyss. She does not know if she can control it, but keeps it sealed as a last resort for the end of the world.
chapters.fullDesc: The Watcher was her secret weapon, a creature of pure abyss bound on her journey through the void. She had never summoned it, never needed to. But as the Sundering worsened, as darkness grew bolder, she knew the time might come. She did not know if she could control it. She did not know if it would obey her, or if it would turn on her, consuming her and everything she loved. But she kept it sealed in the deepest layer of the Kagegasa, a last resort for the end of the world. She hoped she would never need to summon it. She hoped she would find another way, a way that did not risk unleashing something she could not control. But she was a pragmatist. Hope was not a strategy. She prepared for the worst.

chapters.title: The Final Vigil
chapters.shortDesc: Waguri sits alone in the quiet shrine, thinking of Kagura, Hayabusa, and the future. She does not know what will come, but she will keep fighting, waiting, hoping.
chapters.fullDesc: The shrine was quiet. Monsters slept, crystals dimmed, and Waguri sat alone, Koko in her lap, her shadow tails curled around her. She was not sad. She was not afraid. She was at peace. She thought about her sister, about Hayabusa, about the future that might never come. She did not know if she would ever see Kagura again. She did not know if Hayabusa would ever speak the words. She did not know if the shrine would survive the Sundering, if darkness would consume everything, if the light would prevail. But she knew that she would keep fighting. She would keep waiting. She would keep hoping. She was Waguri, the Shadow Keeper, the Monster Summoner of the Inverted Shrine. She was darkness, and darkness was her home. She would not let the light extinguish her.

chapters.title: The Message from Kagura
chapters.shortDesc: A sun priest brings a message: Kagura wishes to meet, not to fight, but to talk. Waguri agrees, her heart leaping at the chance for reconciliation.
chapters.fullDesc: A sun priest came to the shrine, bearing a message. He was young, barely out of training, his hands trembling. 'I bring a message from Priestess Kagura. She wishes to meet you. Not to fight. To talk.' Waguri's heart leaped. 'When? Where?' 'The sun temple, at the next full moon. She will be alone. She asks that you come alone as well.' Waguri nodded. 'Tell her I will come.' The priest fled. Waguri sat in the darkness, her heart pounding. After all these years, her sister was finally willing to talk. She did not know if it was a trap, a trick, or a genuine offer of peace. She did not care. She would go. She would face her sister, not as an enemy, but as a sister. She would try, one last time, to bridge the gap between light and shadow.

chapters.title: The Journey to the Light
chapters.shortDesc: Waguri travels to the sun temple through shadow paths. The light is blinding and painful after years in darkness, but she walks forward, toward her sister.
chapters.fullDesc: The journey to the sun temple was long and dangerous. Waguri traveled through the darkness, using shadow paths only she could see. Koko rode on her shoulder, chittering nervously. Her shadow tails were tucked close, her fox mask pulled down. She reached the temple at dawn, as the sun rose over the mountains. The light was blinding, painful. She had not seen the sun in years, and it hurt. But she walked forward, into the light, toward her sister. Kagura was waiting, alone, as she had promised. She looked tired, thinner than Waguri remembered, her eyes red from weeping. 'Waguri.' 'Kagura.' They stood in silence, light and shadow, two halves of a whole.

chapters.title: The Reconciliation
chapters.shortDesc: Kagura admits she does not understand the darkness but has seen Waguri's face in dreams and knows she is not evil. They embrace, and Waguri's skin burns from the light, but she does not let go.
chapters.fullDesc: 'I don't know if I can accept the darkness,' Kagura said. 'The light priests taught me to fear it, hate it. But I have seen your face in my dreams, and you are not evil. You are just... different.' 'The darkness is not evil. It is just different. It is part of the world, part of the balance. Without shadow, there is no light.' Kagura nodded slowly. 'I am trying to understand. It is not easy.' 'I know. It took me a long time to understand the light. I still do not fully understand it. But I know it is part of you, and I love you, and that is enough.' Kagura wept. Waguri stepped forward and embraced her sister, holding her tightly. The light burned her skin, but she did not let go. They stood there, in the dawn light, two sisters reunited at last.

chapters.title: The Shadow and the Light
chapters.shortDesc: Waguri and Kagura talk for hours, sharing their histories and hopes. They do not agree on everything, but they have found a way to listen. Waguri returns to the shadows, hopeful.
chapters.fullDesc: They talked for hours, about their childhoods, their battles, their hopes for the future. Kagura told Waguri about the light priests' lies and manipulations. Waguri told Kagura about the shrine, the monsters, the darkness that was her home. They did not agree on everything. They probably never would. But they had found a way to talk, to listen, to understand. As the sun set, Waguri said goodbye to her sister and returned to the shadows. She walked through the darkness, Koko on her shoulder, her shadow tails spread wide. She was not sad. She was hopeful. Her sister had not accepted the darkness—not yet. But she had accepted Waguri. That was a start. She would wait. She would always wait. One day, perhaps, light and shadow would be reunited, two halves of a whole, at peace at last.

chapters.title: The Twilight Eternal
chapters.shortDesc: Waguri sits in the quiet shrine, at peace. Her sister has not come home, but she has taken the first step. She closes her eyes, and the darkness holds her. She is home.
chapters.fullDesc: "The darkness is not my enemy. It is my home. My sister is not my enemy. She is my other half. And I will wait for her, as the shadow waits for the light, as the night waits for the dawn. I will wait forever, if I must." — Waguri, speaking to Koko as the sun set on the horizon. The Inverted Shrine was quiet. Monsters slept, crystals dimmed, and Waguri sat alone, Koko in her lap, her shadow tails curled around her. She was not sad. She was not afraid. She was at peace. Her sister had not come home. Not yet. But she had taken the first step, and that was enough. Hayabusa had not spoken the words, but he had made a promise, and that was enough. The shrine was safe. The darkness was strong. And Waguri, the Shadow Keeper, the Monster Summoner of the Inverted Shrine, was content. She closed her eyes, and the darkness held her. The twilight was eternal. And she was home.

chapters.title: A Compendium of Waguri's Powers
chapters.shortDesc: Waguri's abilities: Kagegasa summoning (up to three monsters), Shadow Step teleportation, Legion Unleashed ultimate, and signature monsters (Oni, Tengu, Kappa, Shadow Wolves, Nightmare Steeds, The Watcher).
chapters.fullDesc:
The Nature of Her Power: Waguri's power comes from her bloodline, training, and pact with the darkness. She is tied to the Kagegasa and the fox mask. Her monsters are bound by the pact of the Plum Clan.

Kagegasa Abilities:
- Summoning: Summons up to three monsters at a time. Each attacks independently and shares her stats. On death, leaves a shadow patch that slows enemies.
- Shadow Step: Steps into a shadow and emerges at any other shadow within range, teleporting across the battlefield.
- Legion Unleashed (Ultimate): Opens the Kagegasa fully, releasing all bound monsters. Spawns continuously, slowing enemies. Waguri is invisible and untargetable during the duration.

Signature Monsters:
- Oni Lords (Kurogane, Sekizan, Akuma): Taunt enemies, heavy physical damage.
- Tengu Generals (Seven named for virtues): Fly to target location and explode, area damage and knockback.
- Kappa Legion: Attack quickly, moderate damage, summoned in groups.
- Shadow Wolves: Move swiftly, damage over time.
- Nightmare Steeds: Mounts that fly, run on water, pass through walls.
- The Watcher: Unsummoned secret weapon; can unmake reality, erase targets, destroy cities.

Defensive Abilities:
- Shadow Veil: Wraps in shadows, becoming invisible and faster.
- Plum Blossom Shield: Below a health threshold, releases petals stunning nearby enemies and summoning two oni.
- Shadow Tails: Block attacks, deflect projectiles, sense enemies.

Offensive Techniques:
- Plum Blossom Curse: Basic attacks and skills apply stacks; at five stacks, target takes bonus damage and is feared.
- Tengu's Call: Summons a tengu that explodes at target location.
- Shadow Step Attack: Deals damage to enemies near exit point of Shadow Step.

chapters.title: On the Name 'Waguri'
chapters.shortDesc: Waguri means 'shadow flower' in the old tongue. Her sister Kagura means 'sacred dance of the sun.' Together they are shadow and light, two halves of a whole that was never meant to be divided.
chapters.fullDesc: The name 'Waguri' means 'shadow flower' in the old tongue—a name that reflects her nature as a creature of darkness and beauty. Her mother chose it on the night of her birth, when the lunar eclipse cast its shadow over the shrine. Her sister, Kagura, was named for the sacred dance of the sun. Together, they are shadow and light, yin and yang, two halves of a whole that was never meant to be divided. Waguri does not know if she will ever be reunited with her sister. She does not know if Kagura will ever accept the darkness. She only knows she will keep waiting, keep hoping, keep loving. There is a story among the monsters of the Inverted Shrine about a woman with white hair and shadow tails who sits in darkness, waiting for her sister to come home. The monsters believe she is a goddess. She is not a goddess. She is a sister. A woman who loves, who fights, who forgives. She is the darkness, yes. But the darkness, she has learned, is not evil. It is just alone. She is Waguri, the Monster Summoner of the Inverted Shrine. And she will wait forever, if she must.
